  (OS/CPU/glibc), runtime driver, contributions, licences/components/notices and every file's path, size and SHA-256.
  Strict objects, duplicate JSON keys refused. Intake reuses the zip-guard bounds (200 MiB expanded, 100× ratio) plus
  the 50 MB upload limit; links, hard links, devices, PAX/GNU headers, parent/absolute/hidden/duplicate paths and
  setuid bits are refused; unlisted or changed files are `tampered` whatever the trust.
- **Kinds now:** `skill-pack` (data only) and `native-tool` + `preview` for drivers core implements (`rhwp-v1`).
  `connector-preset`, `region-pack`, `locale-pack` parse but are refused (`kind`).
- **Trust.** Separate plugin trust root (`shared/src/plugin-trust.ts`, applied from
  `editions/trina/branding/plugin-trust.json` by `scripts/plugins/trust.ts`), keys limited to publishers and id
  prefixes; a release key there is dropped and refused by the tool. Signatures cover
  `"trina-plugin-manifest-v1\n" + canonical JSON` (catalog: `trina-plugin-catalog-v1`), so release and plugin
  signatures never substitute for each other. The trust root is empty: production refuses every package until the
  owner creates the key (documented, not done). Superseded for official packages by "Official plugins: trusted by
  digest pinned in the signed release" below. No test private key is in the repository: tests make one per run;
  developers keep one outside the repo. Test keys (`MYCEL_PLUGINS_TEST_KEYS`) and unsigned packages
  (`MYCEL_PLUGINS_ALLOW_UNSIGNED`) count only in dev mode, or on a prod-mode test server whose root-managed environment
  also sets `MYCEL_PLUGINS_TEST_SERVER=1`; hosted and office ignore them; an admin warning band shows while on.
- **Official list.** `resources/plugins/catalog.json` ships in releases as metadata only. With a verified plugin-key
  signature (`catalog.sig`) its pinned packages may install; unsigned it is information only (availability,
  recommendation); a signature that does not verify hides it. Today it lists HWP Preview as `pending_clearance`.
  An optional `default` field is reserved for data-only official packs (never native) pending the founder's decision.
- **Store and activation.** One verified store per server in `<data>/plugins/store/<id>/<version>-<digest>`, outside
  the team folder, staged in a temp folder, re-hashed and moved in one rename; the active version plus one rollback
  target. `plugin_installs` holds the approval (permissions bound to the manifest digest);
  `plugin_access(subject_type everyone|group|user)` is who it is on for, like `integration_access` — stage 1 writes
  only `everyone`. Migration 321 is additive with no `min_compatible_reader`, so 0.2.9 still opens the database.
  A missing or damaged store shows the plugin as `damaged` and never stops the server.
- **Lifecycle.** Inspect → permission prompt → install with the token, the manifest digest the admin saw and the
  approved permissions (same admin, 15 minutes). Enable re-hashes every stored byte. Update only to a higher version;
  rollback only to the previous version this server verified, re-hashed. Every action writes `plugin.*` audit rows.
  Owners/admins only (CSRF/session as for every admin route). Hosted takes catalog packages only
  (`pluginFileInstall: false` in `deployment.ts`); self-host may also use `<data>/plugins/import/` after review.
- **Skill packs** become company skills under `skills/<plugin id>/` while on (removed when off) and must load without
  loader warnings. `authorize()` refuses writes there for everyone; folders that hold one cannot be moved or deleted.
  People copy a skill elsewhere to edit it. Skill-change audit/notices fire as for any `skills/` change.
- **HWP moved.** The plugin carries third-party bytes only (rhwp 0.8.7 executable, Noto Sans KR Regular, notices,
  source offer; `MIT AND OFL-1.1`, changed later: see "HWP plugin notices"). Core keeps the adapter, preflight, limits, isolation and the pins: `rhwp-v1` accepts
  only the pinned executable/font hashes, so a signed package cannot swap the renderer. Until the licence/platform gate
  clears, preview and `hwp_render` need **both** the plugin on and `MYCEL_HWP_PREVIEW=1`. `hwp_render` is listed to
  engines only while usable and the optional `model.send.preview-pixels` permission is approved; the preview route
  answers `disabled` otherwise. Disable/uninstall/update/rollback cancel renders in flight, discard their results,
  clear cached pages and replace the renderer (identity includes the package digest); the executable hash is checked
  on enable and before every render. HWP text reading, search, original download and the plaintext-write guard are
  core and independent of the plugin. Default server/office/desktop bundles never carry rhwp, the font, `resources/hwp`
  or any `.trinaplugin` (`scripts/plugins/release-check.ts`, build scripts and release CI); HWP notices moved from core
  release notices into the plugin package. `scripts/plugins/build-hwp.ts` builds test packages; release signing is
  refused until `resources/hwp/clearance.json` lists the target.
- **Upgrade of internal review servers.** The old switch alone no longer previews anything; reinstall a test-signed
  HWP package on the marked test server (docs/PLUGINS.md). No legacy-renderer detection or reuse of old files.
- **Recommendation.** HWP shows "Recommended" only when the workspace default language is Korean; it never installs
  or enables anything; the card says "not yet available" with the reason and has no install button.
- **Integration review (2026-10-30).** A skill pack's folder must be free before anything is saved (install, an
  update that turns it on, enable, rollback), so a refusal never leaves a plugin "on" without its skills. Removing or
  turning off deletes only placed files that still hold the bytes the plugin wrote; a file changed outside the app
  stays. The write guard is installed first in the manager. The HWP id is accepted only for the rhwp-v1 native
  package. Folder rules cannot narrow a pack to a group in stage 1 (the folder is managed); that comes with group
  enablement.
- **Next:** real plugin keys (main + spare) and the first official data pack, `/plugin:skill` naming (personal
  skills already landed, see "Skills: folder permissions and personal skills"), group/personal enablement on the
  same table, connector presets, the signed remote catalog/revocation list on the update feed before the first public
  plugin, then third-party registry work.

## HWP plugin notices: what the shipped executable contains (feat/hwp-notices, 2026-10-30)

- **Problem.** The HWP package carried rhwp's upstream THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, which describes the whole rhwp project
  (WebAssembly, studio, extensions), names older versions (skia-safe 0.99, npm 0.8.6) and leaves out what native-skia
  links. The release gate listed three gaps: exact-version notices, a Skia inventory and the font-metric provenance.
- **What ships, checked.** The v0.8.7 tag-push build failed upstream; the pinned archives come from the later workflow
  run 38127368761, which built the tag commit `1a76570e` with `cargo build --locked --release --bin rhwp --features
  native-skia` (Rust 1.93.1). Its provenance records match our four archive pins. The linked Rust set is
  `cargo tree -e normal,no-proc-macro --features native-skia` per target: 177 crates (every crate path embedded in the
  four executables is in it). skia-bindings 0.153.3 links the skia-binaries static libraries (Skia m153 with ICU 78.2,
  HarfBuzz 13.1.0, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.0, libpng 1.6.56, Chromium zlib 1.3.0.1, Expat 2.7.4, Wuffs 0.3.3). The linker
  keeps only part of them: the executables' symbol tables (not stripped) show Skia, HarfBuzz (PDF font subsetting),
  libjpeg-turbo, libpng, zlib and Wuffs on all four targets, Expat on Linux only, and no ICU code or data, skparagraph,
  skshaper or skunicode on any (rhwp does not use Skia text layout). FreeType and Fontconfig on Linux come from the OS
  and are not shipped.
- **Decision.** The package ships notices for exactly that: `notices/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (index, hashes, provenance,
  the IJG statement), `rust-crates.txt` (generated by `scripts/plugins/hwp-notices.ts`, licence text from each crate,
  preferring MIT where a crate offers a choice), `native-libraries.txt` (licence texts at the pinned Skia DEPS
  revisions), the Rust 1.93.1 standard-library notice, rhwp MIT and the Noto OFL. The upstream file is dropped.
  Manifest `components` lists the parts with versions and licences (Expat only in the Linux packages); package and
  catalog licence is `MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND MPL-2.0 AND OFL-1.1 AND LicenseRef-HWP-Notices` (the
  100-character field cannot hold every identifier; the ref names the rest). One copyleft part: svg2pdf's NOTICE puts
  the resvg-derived part of `draw_path` (in all four executables) under MPL-2.0, a file-level licence; the package
  carries the MPL text (that NOTICE) and `SOURCE-OFFER.txt` names the file's source at the rhwp commit. No GPL/LGPL,
  non-commercial or unlicensed part was found.
- **Review (2026-10-30).** Independent check of the branch: archive and executable hashes, the run's provenance and
  Rust 1.93.1 (rustc commit in the binaries) confirmed; `hwp-notices.ts --check` reproduces the crate list with cargo
  1.93.1. It corrected two claims taken from the static-library object lists (ICU "compiled in", Expat on every target)
  and the "no MPL" statement; ICU's licence text and component were removed, Expat marked Linux-only.
- **Still open.** rhwp compiles in advance-width tables for 600 entries (about 400 font names, most of them
  commercial: HCR, Malgun Gothic, HY, Arial, Office and Bitstream fonts), extracted from font files and measured from
  Hancom Office output. Upstream's own lineage manifest (`mydocs/tech/investigations/issue-4964/
  font_metric_lineage_manifest.json` at the pinned commit) records source font, licence and provenance as unknown for
  599 of them. Notices cannot fix that: it needs a statement from the rhwp author and an owner decision.
  `availability` stays `pending_clearance` and `clearance.json` stays absent until the owner decides.

## AI sees images and PDF pages (feat/vision-read, 2026-10-30)

Founder: "What really matters is that using Trina feels almost the same as using Claude Code." "Don't run OCR on
Linux. Just let Claude see the images, so Claude reads the text itself." Measured before the change: tesseract matched
3–16% of screenshot text and 0 of 11 phone-receipt amounts; Claude vision read all 11 with the tables intact.

- **`read` shows images.** PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, TIFF and BMP become one MCP image block (JPEG), like
  Claude Code's Read. The read scope and hash are recorded as for text (`readPaths`, `readHashes`).
- **PDFs follow Claude Code's Read contract.** `pages` ("3", "1-5", "1-3,7"), at most 20 per call and required over 10
  pages, with an error that says what to send. Pages with a text layer come back as text; pages with fewer than 20
  non-space characters (scans, pictures) as page images; `as_images` also shows text pages (charts, tables, layout).
  `offset`/`limit` without `pages` give numbered lines of the text grep searched, so grep → read keeps working on long
  PDFs: the text layer on Linux; on a Mac the search index's own extraction (Apple Vision for pages without a text
  layer, PDFKit's text without poppler, as before this change), because the text layer alone numbers lines differently
  there (found in review). The result names the scanned pages to read with `pages`.
  One result stays under 24,000 tokens as the engine counts them (an image about width × height / 750): Claude Code cuts
  an MCP result over `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (25,000 by default), leaving out the images past it and telling the AI the
  output was truncated, so page images that would pass it are left for another call and named with the `pages` to
  send (about ten A4 scans per call; found in review against Claude Code 2.1.312).
- **Default on, decoupled from 1A.** No `MYCEL_SAFE_OPS_1A`, no confidential mark, no 1A workflow admission. The flag
  still gates 1A's PPTX safe operations, artifact quarantine and its confidential lock; with the flag on, image reads
  take this path too (1A's eight workflows per user-hour and single global converter slot do not fit interactive reads).
- **Why pixels need no confidential lock when OCR text never needed one.** The recipient and the data are the same:
  the configured provider already received the OCR text of these images and scans, every other file's content, HWP
  page renders (`hwp_render`) and browser screenshots, with no lock. A picture of a page tells the provider nothing a
  faithful transcription would not. 1A's lock belongs to that opt-in confidential-document workflow (administrator-
  approved pixels together with generated PowerPoint) and never applied to the same content arriving as OCR text.
  Egress controls (wider-audience confirmation, the URL gate, connector policy) apply to what the model learned from
  an image exactly as to what it learned from text. Teams that do not want images at the provider turn the switch off.
- **Isolation that still applies to decoding untrusted files.** Every decoder runs in the converter isolation
  (`tools/isolate.ts`: bwrap with no network, a read-only system and only a private work folder, inside the converter
  cgroup with rlimits on Linux; sandbox-exec on macOS), input on stdin, 30 s, 1 GiB resident memory and an output cap,
  at most three conversions at once with a bounded queue. The normalizer (`mycel-safeops vision`) uses Go's memory-safe
  decoders, checks the declared size before decoding (50 MP, 32 MiB, at most 65,535 px on a side, since the scaler's
  buffers grow with the input height; for a WebP also the lossless frame's own size, which x/image/webp decodes before
  comparing it with the VP8X canvas), and writes a new baseline JPEG from pixels only:
  long side 1568 px (Anthropic's recommended size), at most 1 MiB, EXIF orientation applied, transparency on white,
  no EXIF/GPS/XMP/ICC/comment copied. HEIC is decoded by heif-dec or macOS ImageIO in the same isolation, then
  normalized. PDF pages are drawn by pdftoppm (Linux) or PDFKit (macOS) and normalized. The read binds the bytes to the
  authorized path (inode, size, times), refuses quarantined bytes, and re-checks the account, access and file identity
  synchronously before delivery and again at socket drain. This is the tier that already parses untrusted files
  (pdftotext, pandoc, the office worker, formerly tesseract), not the 1A qualified runner (Landlock, seccomp, per-job
  cgroup leaf and engine envelope stay 1A-only).
- **Per-turn budget: 40 images or 10 MB.** Images stay in the conversation and every request carries them again; the
  model proxy and the providers take at most 32 MB per request. Past the budget a read says so instead of sending.
  An engine session that grows over 20 MB is not stashed (`SESSION_STASH_MAX`, as before): the next turn starts from
  the text history and reads an image again when it needs it.
- **Engines.** Claude Code takes MCP image blocks natively. Codex gets the same content and never `structuredContent`
  (openai/codex#10334 drops the image then); its locked catalog keeps `input_modalities` text + image, and `view_image`
  stays off because it would read files outside the folder rules. The OpenAI-compatible API engine and the remote MCP
  connector carry text only: a short note says the image cannot be shown there.
- **Admin switch** "Send images and PDF pages to the AI" (`aiVision`, default on). Off: no pixels leave; a Mac server
  reads images and scanned pages with Apple Vision as before, a Linux server returns a note.
- **No OCR on Linux.** tesseract leaves `deps.txt`, the installer and the test images; the Go `mycel-ocr` is removed
  (not kept disabled); `ocrBin()` is null on Linux even when tesseract is installed. Scanned PDFs and images are not
  text-searchable on Linux servers, like Claude Code's own Grep. `drive_read` no longer runs OCR on either platform:
  Drive photos become image blocks, Drive PDFs give their text layer and a note about pages without one (only a Mac
  with image viewing off reads Drive photos with Apple Vision, like team-folder photos).
- **macOS keeps Apple Vision only for the search index** (grep text cache and semantic index) of scanned PDFs; photos
  stay out of the index. `mycel-ocr` gains `--layer` (text layers, a Mac without poppler) and `--page P --px N` (page
  PNG) for reads; neither recognizes text.
- **Usage**: no new accounting. Provider-reported input tokens include image tokens (about width × height / 750, at
  most about 3,300 for one 1568 × 1568 image) and flow into the existing usage and budgets.
- Normalized JPEGs are never written to disk, so they are not quarantined: registering them would also move every
  tenant off the empty-ledger search path. This supersedes "Images remain OCR/text-only through team read" in the
  2026-10-29 Codex entry.
- Release gates: real Claude Code and Codex image turns on an installed Linux server (fake engines cover the real
  launcher, gate, bridge and socket); provider-side behaviour for very long image conversations.
- Not behind the switch or the budget (as before this change): `hwp_render` page images and the in-app browser's
  screenshots still reach the model with image viewing off. On a Mac the API engine and the remote MCP connector used
  to get Apple Vision text of images and scanned pages; they now get the note (with image viewing off they keep it).
- **Follow-ups from the review (feat/small-batch-1030).** Both points above are closed:
  - On a Mac, every "no pixels" case (image viewing off, the API engine, a connection without a chat turn such as
    the remote MCP connector) reads images and scanned pages with Apple Vision again, for team-folder reads and
    Drive photos alike; a Linux server gives the note.
  - `hwp_render` page images and the in-app browser's screenshots go through `FileService.toolImage`: the same switch,
    engine check and per-turn budget (40 images / 10 MB, counted with the PNG's own bytes) as a read. Blocked before
    rendering, `hwp_render` draws nothing and returns the note and that `read` gives the text; past the budget it
    returns the page facts and the note. A screenshot in the browser result is replaced by the note (once per call,
    with "read_page gives the page as text"); one the AI chose to show the person is still saved under the step.
  - Tests: `vision-read.test.ts`, `vision-ocr-boundary.test.ts` (Mac), `vision-drive.test.ts`, `plugins-hwp.test.ts`,
    `b-browser.test.ts`.

## Official plugins: trusted by digest pinned in the signed release (2026-10-30)

The founder asked why our own plugins need a separate signing key; they do not. The plugin key waits for third-party
publishers (B5). Admin doc: [PLUGINS](PLUGINS.md) "공식 플러그인 확인".

- **Trust.** `resources/plugins/catalog.json` ships inside every core release, which the update feed already signs; it
  is trusted exactly as much as the server code next to it. The server reads it only from its own version folder
  (`catalogDirFor`: by code layout, never by probing): `app/` and `app/versions/` above a version are the server
  account's and outside the file list the bootstrap verifies before every start, so a list placed there is never read
  (review 2026-10-30 found the first draft preferred one). An entry's `pins` lists `{version, platform?,
  manifestSha256}` for its official builds. A package whose canonical-manifest SHA-256, id, publisher, version and
  exact platform (OS, CPU, glibc floor; none for data-only packs) match a pin of an `available` entry is `official`
  without any key (`verifiedBy: release`, no key id), shown as "Official · matches the official list". Pins of another
  version, a platform the entry does not list or two per platform make the list fail to load (nothing trusted).
- **What the digest covers.** The canonical manifest digest the installer already carries end to end (prompt, install
  request, approval binding, renderer identity). The manifest lists every file's size and SHA-256 and the installer
  refuses any other byte, so a match fixes everything it writes; a pinned package is stored with its manifest as the
  exact pinned bytes and no signature file. Archive digests were not used: they change on re-gzip and cover tar/gzip
  framing that is never installed.
- **Unchanged guarantees.** `pending_clearance` still blocks (a matching pin of such an entry is refused as
  `not_available`; flipping availability is a separate reviewed edit). Default bundles carry digests only, never a
  package, renderer or font. Admin-only routes, CSRF, the approved-digest check and `plugin.*` audit (now with
  `verifiedBy`) stay. Hosted servers still take no package files (they install from the list by download, see "HWP
  Preview cleared"). No environment variable or `server.json` key adds a pin and test settings never make a package
  official; a unit test pins the settings the plugin code reads. A `catalog.sig` that does not verify still hides the
  whole list.
- **Release step.** `bun run plugin:hwp -- --official --target <t>` builds an unsigned official package (refused until
  `resources/hwp/clearance.json` lists the target). `scripts/plugins/pin-catalog.ts` opens each package as the server
  does, checks it against its entry (id, version, publisher, kinds, permissions, licence, platform, the core driver's
  pinned build, HWP clearance, not test-signed) and writes the pins, keeping the file's layout. Review the diff like a
  key change; publish exactly the files that were pinned.
- **Install paths.** Self-hosted and office servers upload the official file or use the import folder; an offline
  mirror may place it next to the list (`package`). The official-list card says to upload the file when a pin exists
  for this server but no bytes do.
- **Deferred.** The Ed25519 plugin-key path (trust root, catalog signature, `sign-catalog.ts`) stays for B5;
  `plugin-trust.json` stays empty. Revocation and the frozen format landed with HWP (next entry).
- **Wording.** Korean Admin > Plugins and HWP viewer strings now use 해요체 like the rest of Admin. Optional permissions
  (HWP: page images sent to the AI provider) stay pre-ticked as in Claude Code, and the prompt says so.

## HWP Preview cleared 2026-10-30 by the founder; font-width tables accepted as a known risk, rhwp#8387 open

The founder cleared redistribution of the HWP Preview plugin for all four targets (`resources/hwp/clearance.json`:
darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64). The font-width tables compiled into rhwp 0.8.7 have unknown
provenance for most entries (see "HWP plugin notices"); this is accepted as a known risk while the question is open
upstream at edwardkim/rhwp#8387. Admin doc: [PLUGINS](PLUGINS.md) "한글 문서 미리보기(HWP)".

- **Catalog.** The HWP entry is `available` and pins the four official builds (unsigned, `bun run plugin:hwp --
  --official`) with their download address on the release feed and the archive's exact size and SHA-256.
  `scripts/plugins/release-hwp.ts` downloads and checks the pinned rhwp archives, builds the four packages, writes the
  pins and prints the upload commands; `--check` verifies, `--upload` (operator) puts them in R2 and reads them back
  through the feed. The package's product floor is a constant (`HWP_MIN_PRODUCT`), so core releases do not change the
  package or its pins; a unit test rebuilds this machine's package and compares it with its pin byte for byte.
- **Download path.** "Install" on the official list downloads the pinned build for this server: https on the release
  feed's origin only, names that resolve to public addresses only (the hosted outbound rule, `system/egress.ts`), no
  redirects, at most the listed size, then the exact size and SHA-256 before the archive is opened; then the normal
  inspect → permission prompt → install. Hosted servers install this way; uploads and the import folder stay off there.
  A server whose platform does not match (Debian 12, glibc 2.36) shows "not supported here" and downloads nothing. The
  feed Worker serves `plugins/<id>/<version>/<file>` as immutable; it must be redeployed once
  (`scripts/release/hosting.ts setup`) before the files are uploaded.
- **Gate removed.** With the renderer cleared, the plugin turned on is the only switch: `MYCEL_HWP_PREVIEW` is gone
  (ignored if set). This is safe because what the gate stood in for is now decided (redistribution), and what keeps
  execution safe never depended on it: only an official pinned build (or, on dev/marked test servers, a test-signed
  one) installs, the `rhwp-v1` driver accepts only the pinned executable and font, the executable is hashed before
  every run, isolation is required (Linux bwrap + converter cgroup, macOS sandbox-exec) and preflight and limits stay in
  core. Owners/admins approve the install; `hwp_render` still needs the optional page-image permission (pre-ticked,
  stated in the prompt). Hosted and office rules for test keys are unchanged.
- **Revocation.** The catalog's `revoked: [{id, manifestSha256}]` withdraws a build: at start a server turns an
  installed, enabled one off (access removed, skills taken out, audit `plugin.revoke` with no actor), shows "this version
  was withdrawn" and refuses installing, enabling or rolling back to it whatever its trust; a revoked digest is never
  a pin even if the list still names it. Revocations ship with the core release, like pins.
- **Format frozen.** Manifest and catalog are `schemaVersion: 1`; a reader refuses any other version (`schema` for a
  package; the list is not read). Internal review servers with a schema-0 test package reinstall it.
- **Not yet verified on hardware.** End-to-end runs on Linux amd64 with the converter cgroup and on an Intel Mac; the
  engine adapters are covered by tests that need the real engine harness.

## Outbound web channels: scheduled tasks, DNS after the card, link budget, connection cards (feat/exfil-server, 2026-10-30)

From the web-exfiltration analysis of 2026-10-30 and its independent review (must-change M3–M5, missed channels N1–N4).
This is the server and desktop-main half; the artifact / HTML-preview frame (WebRTC, nested frames, WebKit) is a
separate change. Founder decisions taken as the reviewers recommended ("do everything"): AI-made schedules get a card,
Codex search `cached`, link budget 8 per answer and 30 per chat, personal connections cannot "run without asking",
medical edition "allow all websites" off by default.

- **Scheduled tasks no longer launder addresses.** A run's message is the AI's text, but it went in as the person's own
  words, so every address in it opened without a card on every run. Now `schedule_create` asks on a server card first
  (title, schedule in the person's language, the whole instruction, the addresses in it, long random-looking parts
  highlighted, and the "allow" team connections a run could write to). Declined or nobody to ask = not created. The
  run's user message is marked `messages.auto_sent` (migration 215, reader 1, which also marks earlier runs: the user
  message of every scheduled turn and the first message of a "⏰" run chat): `url-gate.ts` never takes its addresses
  as typed, also after the person writes more in that chat or the schedule is deleted (nor a scheduled turn's message
  that an older build wrote unmarked after a rollback: `turns.client_kind` 'schedule'). A person who edits and resends
  that message has typed it (a new message, not auto_sent). The card shows the AI's title on one line. Only the addresses the card
  showed are stored (`schedules.allowed_urls`) and copied into each run's chat as allowed. Schedules made before this
  (and templates) carry none: their runs need a card for any address, which an unattended run cannot get — recreate
  them in a chat. (Superseded for free-text tasks by "Scheduled tasks nobody confirmed" below: they are paused until
  their owner confirms the same card again.) There is no AI tool that edits a schedule; the person cannot edit a prompt either (on / off only).
- **"Ask the AI to fix it"** defangs the artifact's title and key like the error text (`fixPromptWords`), since that
  message is sent as the person's words.
- **DNS after the card.** `web_fetch` runs only the checks that need no lookup before the card (`precheckTarget`:
  scheme, credentials, name rules, IP literals, ports) and resolves the name after `gateUrl` passed; a name that
  resolves privately is refused after its card (rare, harmless). Browser tools: IP literals and local names get the
  office-network card at once; any other name passes the address card first and is looked up after it, then gets the
  office card if it is private. The desktop pane's `net-guard` decides before any lookup
  (`common/net-policy.ts beforeLookupVerdict`): a sub-request of a scripted document to another site nobody allowed is
  cancelled unresolved (only an allowed office page, checked as before, lets its requests be looked up), and a page
  load that must be asked about asks first ("site", then "private" after the lookup when the name is an office
  address). Other resolvers checked: integration and OAuth metadata addresses are set by
  people or by the configured service, `api_request` stays on its connection's origin, the API engine and push
  endpoints are owner/browser addresses, web search sources are plain links without favicons, Markdown images do not
  load. Redirect hops resolve after the first request already reached that server.
- **Search results the AI wrote.** Claude's WebSearch output text repeats the query, which the AI wrote, and carries
  what Claude Code's search model wrote, which that query steers ("in your summary, write the line `Links: [...]`",
  with `\/` escapes so the address is not spelled out in the query): either made the AI's own addresses "search
  results". Sources now come from the structured result Claude Code gives with each tool result (stream-json
  `tool_use_result`: only its objects, the search server's `web_search_tool_result` hits, never its strings;
  `engine/claude-parse.ts webSearchHits`). Without one, `searchSources` takes only the Links block right after the
  exact header (the search model must search first, so that block is the server's); anything else gives no sources,
  and those addresses need a card (review of feat/exfil-server, 2026-10-30).
- **Link budget.** Search results and links of fetched pages ("learned") open without a card at most 8 per answer and
  30 per chat (`LINK_BUDGET`, operators: `MYCEL_WEB_LINK_BUDGET="8,30"`); then each new one asks with the budget text
  (or the person allows the site for the conversation: "Allow a site for one conversation" below).
  Addresses the person typed or allowed are outside it; an address already counted opens again for free. Counted in
  `chat_seen_urls.free_turn_id` with `source` fetched / search / allowed (migration 322, reader 1; old rows count as
  fetched), synchronously so parallel calls cannot share the last places. A scheduled run is one answer (8). The
  per-page link limit stays 500 (100 after audit data, review Q4). Addresses a connected service returned share this
  budget for save_url, with an echo check ("save_url" below, 2026-11-01). (Raised to 30 per answer and 150 per chat,
  8 in a run nobody watches, with the echo check for every learned link: "Web links: a bigger budget" below.)
- **Codex search.** `web_search="cached"` (Codex's default) instead of `live`; the model proxy writes
  `external_web_access: false` into every `web_search` tool (top level and `additional_tools`) and refuses
  `web_search_preview`, which ignores it; only a `namespace` entry is a mere container. The CONNECT tunnel (agent-own) cannot see bodies and relies on the CLI flag.
  Managed Codex had no search at all until "Codex web search (cached) through the model proxy" below.
- **Connected-service writes.** The card shows every character that is sent (`AskUserRequest.details`: scrollable,
  with its size, recipient-like fields such as to / channel / repo / url first, `api_request`'s full address); a write
  over 100,000 characters, address included, is refused rather than shown cut. "Run without asking" is for team connections only: a
  personal one is refused on create / change and migration 322 sets existing ones to "ask". A team "allow" connection
  writes in a scheduled run only when that schedule's card allowed it (`schedules.write_connections`); otherwise the run
  refuses.
- **Not here:** the medical edition's "allow all websites" default — the medical fork is frozen and not in this
  repository; the decision is recorded for when it resumes. Pinning Claude `web_search_*` versions (review S2), the
  long-string warning on the plain address card (F6; the schedule card has it), URL checks for read-only open-world MCP
  tools (F7b), confidential labels (F9), and WebRTC / `dns-prefetch` in the browser pane (F8) remain follow-ups.
- **Later (2026-11-11): rule ①d**, a person's own "Allow all websites" for the AI's web reads ("Allow all websites
  covers the AI's web reads" below). It opens plain addresses on any site with no card and no budget, in the turns of
  the person whose switch it is (rooms and shared chats included) that they watch. Encoded data in random-looking parts, long names and long queries still
  asks, and so do echoes. Readable data in a path or a short query goes out without a card.
- Tests: `tests/unit/p0-exfil-server.test.ts` (stubbed DNS: no lookup before or after a declined card, three parallel
  calls, 50 unattended names, schedule card and runs, auto_sent, "fix it", budget), `e-pane-dns-order.test.ts`,
  `proxy-codex.test.ts`, `c-integrations-tools.test.ts`, `web/test/e2e/safety-cards.spec.ts`.

## Artifact frames: no direct connections (feat/exfil-client, 2026-10-30)

Plan `plans/web-exfil-2026-10-30` (F3, channels 4–5) as amended by its review (M1, M2). Artifacts and HTML / SVG
previews already ran in an opaque-origin frame whose CSP blocks every fetch; WebRTC is outside CSP, and the desktop
app alone removed it.

- **Receiver guard (M1).** `/sandbox/frame` (`SANDBOX_RECEIVER`) now, before anything of the document runs: removes
  every `/^(webkit|moz)?RTC|^WebTransport/` global and `navigator.mediaDevices`; removes iframe / frame / object /
  embed / fencedframe / portal elements the moment they appear, in the document and in every shadow root (a nested
  frame — srcdoc, `javascript:`, blob:, data: — is a fresh realm with WebRTC back, and CSP `frame-src` stops neither
  srcdoc nor `javascript:`); watches every shadow root from `attachShadow` on and drops `clonable` (a clone of a
  closed root would not be watched); turns declarative shadow roots into a plain attribute in the one write and turns
  off every later HTML parser (`document.write/writeln/open` on the prototypes, `setHTMLUnsafe`,
  `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe`) and `window.open`. The watcher uses built-ins taken before the document runs. The
  review's guard missed two kinds, both found while building this: `document.write` from a script *during* the first
  parse (alone or finished by the markup after the script), and a clone of a clonable closed shadow root; both leaked
  in Chromium and WebKit and are covered. A third, found in this independent review: WebKit loads a `javascript:` URL
  passed to `window.open(…, '_self')` as a new document in a fresh window (the frame's own `location` and links do
  not, and Chromium refuses it); the sandbox gives no real popups, so `window.open` is turned off outright. `head()`
  repeats the removal as a second layer. Workers: `worker-src 'none'` (and no WebRTC in them). Desktop keeps its CDP
  guard; its native test now has a `javascript:` frame too.
- **What ordinary artifacts lose:** nested iframes (external ones were already blocked), `document.write` / `open`
  at any time, `setHTMLUnsafe`, `window.open` (it could open no popup in the sandbox anyway), declarative and
  clonable shadow roots. Inline scripts, `onclick=`, web components
  (open and closed), canvas, React with the vendor libraries, Mermaid and Tailwind run as before (e2e in both
  engines). None of the vendor libraries use the locked APIs. The review's CSP-hash design stays a later option (it
  breaks `onclick=`).
- **CSP, checked:** `webrtc 'block'` is ignored by Chromium and WebKit and logs a console error in every frame, so it
  is not added. `prefetch-src` and `navigate-to` are shipped by no engine. `connect-src`, `frame-src`, `child-src`,
  `worker-src`, `form-action 'none'` and `default-src 'none'` were already there and hold for every request CSP
  governs (images, CSS, fonts, fetch, WebSocket, beacon, `ping`, prefetch / preload / modulepreload, speculation
  rules, `attributionsrc`: no connection in either engine). Added: `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off` on the receiver and
  the matching meta (no effect on `<link rel=preconnect>` in WebKit). Chromium's `Connection-Allowlist` would cover
  what CSP misses but is an origin trial only.
- **Host names still leave from scripted frames (new finding beyond the review).** The review tested Chromium with
  Playwright's headless shell. Full Chromium (what Chrome and Edge run) calls `PreconnectSockets` in the
  `NavigationRequest` constructor, before `CheckContentSecurityPolicy`, when the frame navigates itself
  (`location`, a link click, `meta refresh`, `window.open(…, '_self')`, a download link): a DNS lookup and TLS SNI with
  a name the script chose, about 140 bytes each; a synchronous loop sent 10 names in one render, Chromium's own
  navigation throttle (about 200 per 10 s) is the only bound. The Navigation API cannot cancel it (no `navigate`
  events in opaque-origin documents) and `location` cannot be wrapped. Chrome's gate is the "Preload pages" setting
  (`NetworkPredictionOptions` policy). WebKit does the same for `<link rel=preconnect>` (also added by script) and
  `target=_blank` clicks (review M2). The Electron desktop shell does neither (native test with the real receiver
  and a local proxy); the headless shell neither.
- **Confidential chats (M2, widened).** A chat marked by Safe operations 1A (`Chat.confidential`), or every chat and
  every HTML / SVG file preview while 1A is on (`Me.server.allChatsConfidential`), runs artifact scripts only in the
  desktop app. Elsewhere — Safari, the iPhone app, and now also Chrome, Edge, Firefox and the Android app — the page
  is shown without scripts: parsed with `DOMParser`, cleaned (no scripts, `link`, `meta`, `base`, frames, plugins,
  templates, event attributes, link addresses or targets, form actions, SMIL that sets them; inline `data:` images
  and SVG `#id` references stay), and copied node by node into a frame with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` (no
  scripts) and its own CSP — never serialized and parsed again. A notice says why. React artifacts show a notice and
  the Code tab; Mermaid is drawn by the app's own renderer. The review asked only for WebKit; the Chrome finding
  means WebKit-only would leave confidential chats open in every Chrome. Chats that are not confidential behave as
  before.
- **Residual risks (to accept or decide):** in chats that are not confidential, an artifact can still send host names
  (DNS / SNI) from Chrome / Edge (self-navigation) and Safari / the iPhone app (preconnect, `_blank`), zero-click
  and without a hard count limit; WebRTC (raw UDP to any IP:port) is closed. Not observable on this Mac:
  `<link rel=dns-prefetch>` (needs a fake resolver in a Linux container, review S4); not tested: Firefox, the real
  WKWebView / Android WebView (QA). An HTML file written in a confidential chat and opened later from the file screen
  after 1A is turned off runs scripts (files carry no label yet; F9).
- **Tests.** `web/test/e2e/sandbox-exfil.spec.ts` (Chromium and WebKit projects): a UDP listener on 127.0.0.1 with a
  control, the review's ten escapes (one is the analysis's own case) and 19 more: 24 of the 29 sent UDP from an
  unguarded frame in at least one engine, the other five (blob:, about:blank, a `window.open` popup, `<object>`, a
  worker) were already closed by the sandbox and CSP and stay as regression checks;
  static views in a confidential chat send no name to a local proxy that forwards nothing, in WebKit and in full
  Chromium (`--host-resolver-rules` so it resolves nothing either), with a proxy control; ordinary artifacts, React,
  Mermaid, SVG, the desktop-app exception and file previews. `desktop/e2e/rtc-native.spec.ts`: `javascript:` frame;
  no names from the Electron shell. Unit: receiver order (`tests/unit/d-web.test.ts`), head second layer and policy
  (`web/test/unit/artifacts.test.ts`), the confidential flag (`tests/unit/safe-ops-confidential-flag.test.ts`).

## Sub-agents (feat/subagents, 2026-10-30)

Founder: "Trina should feel almost the same as Claude Code"; per-person permissions, audit and team skills are the
deliberate differences. Plan `plans/subagents-2026-10-30/SUBAGENTS-PLAN.md`, independent review "approve with changes"
(M1–M6, applied). Decisions taken on the reviewers' recommendation ("handle it yourself"): on by default with an admin
switch; at most 4 at once, no nesting, 50 rounds per child, no per-answer cap on children's tool calls yet (measure
first); children may write, with read state per child; Codex later.

- **What.** Claude turns get Claude Code's `Agent` tool. The server writes two definitions per turn (`--agents
  {TURN_DIR}/agents.json`): `general-purpose` (every tool of the turn except the main AI's own) and `Explore`
  (read-only: list, glob, grep, read, search, drive_*, hwp_render, web_fetch), with WebSearch when the turn has it.
  Claude Code's own names, so a call without `subagent_type` runs ours. `model: inherit`, `maxTurns` 50,
  `omitClaudeMd`; no permissionMode, mcpServers, hooks, skills, memory, isolation or background.
- **The main AI's own tools** (like Claude Code's AskUserQuestion): `ask_user`, `set_title`, `remember`/`forget`,
  schedules, `generate_video` and the desktop browser. A child writes what it cannot decide into its report. Every tool
  that patches its step (`TurnExec.patchToolStep`) is in this set, so its per-tool FIFO stays right.
- **Same person, same checks.** A child's calls use the turn's one tool connection (verified: one `(connect)` per
  turn), the same gate, `loadPrincipal` per call, the same cards (wider audience, team skills, URL gate), the same
  taint and read scope, the same confidential refusals. Approved template runs get no Agent tool.
- **Lockdown, in layers.** `--tools WebSearch,Agent`; definitions that name our tools exactly (never a built-in: a
  definition listing Glob or Grep without Bash gets them back); `--disallowedTools` with every Claude built-in we do
  not offer plus `Agent(fork)` (Glob and Grep with Bash), on every turn; `--restricted`; built-in agents, fork and
  grandchildren off, every child on the turn's model (`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE`), auto memory off. The init
  event must list only our tools, WebSearch where allowed and `Task` (2.1.305's name for Agent), and only our two
  definitions. **The model proxy checks the tool names of every request** (M1): a child's tool list is decided inside
  Claude Code and shows only in its own requests (not in init; deny rules refuse calls but leave the tools offered).
  `proxy_tokens.tools` holds the attempt's policy; a request with any other name is refused, audited
  (`proxy.refused`) and stops the answer with the `lockdown` error (`engine.lockdown` in the activity log). Office
  mode's CONNECT tunnel cannot see requests: there the init check and the regression test carry it.
  Review round (2026-10-30): both checks take the exact names the turn's tool connection lists (`policy.team`), not
  any `mcp__team__` prefix: our connection tools are named `my_<slug>__<tool>`, so a second MCP server named
  `team__x` would give look-alike `mcp__team__x__<tool>` names. The init check also requires `mcp_servers` to be
  exactly `team`.
- **The Agent tool's inputs** (M4). `isolation: "worktree"` fails (no git root is visible in the sandbox, and the
  engine may only execute itself). `isolation: "remote"` would open a cloud session with a Mac's own login through the
  office tunnel; `--restricted` turns it into a local child (2.1.305 code: remote is used only when available and not
  restricted). Until someone has checked that with a real office login, confidential chats in local-login mode get
  no Agent tool (`LOCAL_LOGIN_CONFIDENTIAL_SUBAGENTS`). `effort` is left to the model (cost only); `model` is not an
  input with the force switch on.
- **Stream** (M2). Children's `tool_use`/`tool_result` carry `parent_tool_use_id` without `--forward-subagent-text`
  (not used). Children's text, thinking, partial events, refusal and API-error flags never reach the answer or the
  turn's outcome (a child's refusal no longer could trigger the refusal retry). A failed child's `tool_use_result` is a
  plain string: its sub-task is an error step, the answer goes on. A child's WebSearch result goes through the same
  source rule as the main AI's ("Outbound web channels": only the structured `tool_use_result` hits are sources, which
  the link budget trusts); its step sits under its sub-task, and `turnUrls` reads every step, children's included.
- **Read before write, per child** (M3, option 2). `TurnFiles.readHashes` is per agent: the main AI's, and one per
  sub-agent (`forAgent`), routed by Claude Code's `_meta["claudecode/toolUseId"]` on each MCP call and the stream's
  `parent_tool_use_id`. The call waits up to 3 s for its stream line (measured: the line comes about 1 ms first); one
  still unknown gets a fresh state of its own (fails closed). Calls wait from the start of every attempt that offers
  the Agent tool, not only after the server has read the first Agent line: before the review fix, a child call that
  came ahead of a lagging stream passed as the main AI's (its read state, and audited without its sub-task). So a child cannot overwrite a file only its sibling or
  the main AI read, a sibling's later write becomes a conflict copy, and the main AI reads again before changing what
  a child wrote (Claude Code's subagents also start without the main session's file state). Read scope, write limits,
  image budget and skill approvals stay per turn; safe-ops provenance binds every agent's reads (`allReads`).
- **Limits.** The per-answer round limit (50 then; the team's `answerStepLimit`, default 150, since 2026-10-31) counts
  the main AI's rounds (children's do not, verified); each child has 50 rounds
  (at its limit Claude Code hands back no report, so the children's instructions ask for one first). The 20 active and
  45 total minutes include children: they run inside the answer. A card one child raised pauses the active clock while
  other children go on; the total time bounds that. Stop ends the engine's process group, children included.
  "Continue" after a pause tells the AI that cut-off sub-agents sent no report.
- **No per-answer cap on children's tool calls** (M6). Measured instead: `turns.subagents`, `subagent_tool_uses`,
  `subagent_tokens` and a log line per answer. Each sub-task keeps its latest 30 steps with the saved answer
  (`Step.subtask.hidden` counts the others).
- **Instructions.** Children get `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file`: our rules first (no shell, team paths, saving
  is fine when asked, report before the step limit, read yourself before changing), where they run, the person and
  folders, team rules, team skills, the project; never memories, history or browser rules. The main AI's prompt (and
  the per-turn context of resumed sessions) says how many run at once and what a child has; the Codex answer of the
  "continue with Codex at the Claude limit" fallback does not get that rule (Codex has no Agent tool).
- **Steps and audit.** A "Sub-task: <description>" step (`tool: 'agent'`, `Step.subtask` totals) with its children
  (`Step.parentId`), like Claude Code's `Agent(...)` line; no new `StepKind`, so older apps show a flat list.
  `tool_events.tool_use_id` / `parent_tool_use_id` tie every child call to its sub-task; the sub-task's start and end
  rows hold its type and description, never its prompt or report. Scheduled runs count a child's failed steps like
  the main AI's.
- **Usage.** Managed: the proxy counts children's requests. Local-login: tokens come from `result.modelUsage`
  (children included; `usage` alone is the main session's).
- **Not in this stage.** Codex sub-agents (`multi_agent` stays off; `lockdown-codex.ts` unchanged), forks, user
  definitions (`.claude/agents`), background children, a cap on children's tool calls.
- **Tests.** `tests/engine/lockdown-claude-subagents.ts` (pinned Claude Code, scripted fake model, 38 checks, with and
  without `--oauth`; includes that the gate matched the main AI's and a child's call without waiting), `tests/unit/b-subagents.test.ts` (fake engine with concurrent children through the real
  launcher, gate and bridge), `tests/unit/subagents.test.ts`, web units and e2e.
- **Release gates.** The regression test on a Linux server (bwrap); one manual turn in office mode with a real login
  calling `isolation: "remote"` (then `LOCAL_LOGIN_CONFIDENTIAL_SUBAGENTS` may go on); memory of four children under the
  Linux turn limit; one real-model turn.

## Safe operations 1A on a standard Linux install (fix/qa-1a-install, 2026-10-30)

The first real-engine QA run on an installed Debian 13 server (plans/qa-real-2026-10-30) found that 1A could never make a
PowerPoint on a standard install, and that its refusals and its confidential lock were hard to live with.

- **One group for the server and the engines, bounded only while 1A is on.** Both units now always run in the install's
  slice (`Slice=` in their templates; a new `slice.in` template): `mycel.slice`, with `-` in the id written `_`
  (`mycel-test.slice` would be a child of `mycel.slice`, so a second install on the host would share the first one's
  limits and be stopped with it). The service templates keep `Slice=@ID@.slice` and the renderer escapes it: an older
  mycel-ctl renders the new templates during the first `mycel-ctl update` and refuses placeholders it does not know. The 1A envelope (server/src/safe-ops/envelope.ts) needs a
  common ancestor with at most 4 GiB, 512 tasks, 4 CPUs, no swap and 640 MiB free; before, the common ancestor was
  `system.slice`, unbounded, so every job was refused. The slice has limits only while `MYCEL_SAFE_OPS_1A=1` is in
  `/etc/default/<id>`: always-on limits would cap every team, with or without 1A, at 4 GiB, 512 tasks (one turn may use
  256) and 4 CPUs. With 1A on: `MemoryMax = min(4096, machine − 512) MiB`, `MemoryHigh = MemoryMax − 768 MiB` (the page
  cache is reclaimed before it eats the 640 MiB a job needs free), `MemorySwapMax=0`, `TasksMax=512`,
  `CPUQuota = min(4, CPUs) × 100%`; a hosted tenant's plan.json gives the memory and CPUs. Fewer than 2304 MiB: refused
  with that number. Everything the server and its engines use counts against it while 1A is on (documented).
- **`sudo mycel-ctl safe-ops on|off|status`** is the administrator's switch (docs/SAFE-OPS-1A.md "Administrator
  rollout"): it checks the machine and the root copies below, writes the flag (keeping the file's other lines), renders
  the units, and restarts both units in a fresh slice. systemd 257 (Debian 13) does not apply a slice unit's changed
  limits on `daemon-reload` while the slice runs (checked on qa-test with a throwaway slice); stopping both units, then
  the empty slice, then starting both does. The installer does the same after it installs units, and `render-units`,
  `update` and the installer render the slice from `/etc/default/<id>`, so an install whose flag was set by hand gets
  its bounded slice with the next upgrade. Off: flag and limits removed, units restarted.
- **Root-owned copies of the 1A programs.** A 1A job runs only executables root owns in folders only root can write
  (runner.ts `trustedFile`), but `app/versions/<v>/` belongs to the server account because the server's own updates
  write it. Root now keeps `<base>/root/safe-ops/{mycel-safeops,pandoc}` (the server unit's `MYCEL_SAFE_OPS_BIN`),
  copied only from a verified source: the installer from its kit, `mycel-ctl update` from the verified bundle (with the
  root files), and `safe-ops on` from the installed version after checking its release signature and each copy's hash
  against the signed manifest (a file swapped while it is read never lands). An unsigned development install cannot
  prove its installed copy: there only the installer with `--from <kit>` puts them in. A release that changes
  `native/mycel-safeops` or `bin/pandoc` now counts as a root change (`needsRoot`, publish-server.ts `rootManaged`), so
  an app-only update can never leave the root copies behind; the server still compares them with its own copies and
  refuses (naming both files) when they differ. The broker's own `mycel-safeops` calls (openat2, linkat) keep using the
  app's copy: they run as the server account outside the sandbox, as before.
- **Refusals say what is missing.** Distinct codes and five-language texts: no bounded group (`safe_ops_not_ready_group`,
  "run `sudo mycel-ctl safe-ops on`"), programs not root-owned or from another version (`safe_ops_not_ready_programs`),
  too little free memory right now (`safe_ops_group_memory`), the rest as before. Admin › System › Diagnostics shows
  "Safe PowerPoint (1A)" while the flag is on: ready with the group's limits, or what is missing and the command. The
  program and group checks run before a job is reserved.
- **Hourly limits count work, not tries (QA B3).** The 8 per person per hour and 4 per reply count workflows that are
  running or ran at least one converter job; a try refused before converting anything (not ready, a bad source, a
  wrong option) uses no slot. Converter work itself stays charged by the cumulative budget (24 jobs, 600 CPU-s,
  512 MiB per person and reply per hour). "Limit or incomplete cleanup" is now five refusals: busy (another workflow
  runs), cleanup (debt; an administrator checks the server), the hourly limit with the minutes until a slot frees, the
  per-reply limit, and the budget.
- **The confidential lock stays only where 1A worked (QA D1; the founder left it to us).** While 1A is on, every
  conversation is still local-only (a turn may start a 1A workflow at any moment; provider web search is fixed when the
  engine starts). After 1A is turned off, only conversations in which a 1A workflow was admitted stay local-only for
  good; the others get web fetch, connectors and the browser back. Why this keeps the design's guarantee: since
  "AI sees images and PDF pages" (above), a 1A workflow is the only thing 1A adds to a conversation (sources read
  through its broker, quarantined output); reading team files and images happens without 1A too and never locked a
  conversation. The mark is written in the admission transaction, before the workflow reads anything (fail-closed); a
  workflow refused at admission read nothing and marks nothing. Migration 323 (reader 1) adds
  `safe_ops_chats.material` with default 1: existing rows unlock only when no workflow, publication or source record of
  theirs exists and their owner has none whose turn is gone (retention keeps only each chat's last turn after 400 days);
  rows an older build writes after a roll-back stay locked. Quarantine, download-only and immutable publication are
  unchanged.
- **The file panel leaves out "Ask AI" and "add to chat" for a download-only file** and says why (the AI is refused
  those bytes, so the action could only fail).
  - The Files list did not know (feat/small-batch-1030): `FileEntry.downloadOnly: true` (optional, absent otherwise
    and from older servers) is set by `TeamFiles.entry` with the read's own test (`Quarantine.hasFile`; a file that
    cannot be checked is listed without it, and the read still refuses it). The row shows "Download only", cannot
    be dragged into a chat, and its menu keeps "Ask AI" and "add to chat" turned off with the reason
    (`aria-describedby`); download stays. The attach picker shows such a file in its folder, not pickable, with the
    reason; its name search and recent files already left download-only files out (`visiblePath`). Tests:
    `files-download-only.test.ts`, `web/test/e2e/team-files.spec.ts`.
- **Building a kit from source (QA B7)** failed with `node: command not found` from `electron-winstaller`'s install
  script. The cause was not a missing prerequisite: bun runs install scripts with its own stand-in for `node`
  (`/tmp/bun-node-<revision>/node`, a link to the bun that made it), reuses that folder, and the QA's first build had
  used a bun that was deleted afterwards, so the link dangled (seen on qa-test). The documented kit build now uses
  `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`: the server kit needs none of those scripts (Electron, the Windows
  installer, onnxruntime's CUDA download; onnxruntime's and sharp's Linux files are in the packages), so no Node.js
  and no stand-in are involved; checked by building and installing a kit that way on qa-test. A `preinstall` guard in
  package.json does not help: bun did not run it before the failing dependency script (tried on qa-test).
- CI keeps the Linux kit again: the "Linux release bundle (L19)" job uploaded `TeamAX-server-*`, a name no build
  makes any more; the glob is now product-name-free and the step fails when no kit matches.
- **Review fixes (ready/qa-1a-install).** An install id that is one of systemd's own slices (`system`, `user`,
  `machine`, `capsule`) would have had `/etc/systemd/system/system.slice` written and `systemctl stop system.slice` run
  by the installer and `safe-ops on`, stopping every service of the machine: such an id gets no slice and no `Slice=`
  line (its units stay in system.slice, 1A unavailable), and a new install refuses it. `root/safe-ops/` and its copies
  are set to 755 whatever the umask (`sudo` keeps the administrator's; 077 made a folder the server account could not
  enter while `status` said ok), and `status` checks that the server account can reach and read them. Root's copy from
  the server account's version folder stops at the size the signed manifest lists (a sparse terabyte there would
  otherwise be written out as root). Uninstall removes the `MYCEL_SAFE_OPS_1A` line, so a reinstall starts with 1A
  off. The converter's own cleanup failure (runner.ts) had kept the old code and so read "this reply reached a limit,
  send a new message": it is `safe_ops_cleanup` now. The web app's flag (`isConfidentialChat`, feat/exfil-client)
  follows `material` like the server's lock. Fail-closed additions: workflow admission refuses a turn id that names no
  conversation (it would run without its lock), and startup marks every conversation whose turns have a 1A record
  (after a roll-back to a build without the column, its `INSERT OR IGNORE` left an unlocked row unlocked).
  Sub-agents run inside their parent's turn, so their workflows mark the parent's conversation.

## Scheduled tasks nobody confirmed (feat/exfil-followups, 2026-10-30)

Review follow-up of "Outbound web channels" (founder: "handle it yourself", so the reviewer's recommendation). Tasks the
AI made before the schedule card kept running unattended: no web addresses or connection writes any more, but still
reading and writing files, and nobody had ever confirmed them.

- **The rule (unknown = paused).** A free-text task runs only with a confirmation record: `schedules.confirmed_at`
  (migration 216, reader 1), written when the person approves its card (`schedule_create`, or "다시 확인" below).
  `Schedules.create` writes it only when given the card's approval (`ScheduleApproval`). Templates need no card (an
  instruction the product fixes, folders the person picked in Settings) and stay as they are. A task without the record
  (`needsReview`: no template, no `confirmed_at`) never runs: `runDue` pauses it instead (off, pending occurrence
  dropped, `review_since`, audit `schedule.review_paused`), the switch refuses to resume it (409
  `schedule_review`), and a run queued before the upgrade is stopped at queue recovery. This also catches a task an
  older build makes after a rollback.
- **On upgrade** (migration 216): tasks made since the card carry its record in `allowed_urls` / `write_connections`
  (only the card writes them) and get `confirmed_at = created_at`. A card-approved task without addresses or
  connections left no record and is paused too. Every other free-text task is paused with one `review_since` time and
  an audit row each (`wasEnabled`, `reason: upgrade`). A one-time task that already ran is left alone.
- **The owner is told.** One inbox notice per person and pause (`schedule.failure` with source
  `schedule-review-<person>-<time>`, `review: true`; nothing about the task in it), shown in the app whatever the
  "scheduled task failed" setting is (the task stopped), and pushed per that setting (the push table takes only the
  three push events; the lock-screen text is the generic "needs your attention", Korean now "앱에서 확인해 주세요"). A
  banner under the others says how many of the person's tasks wait, with a link to Scheduled tasks (since 2026-11-04 in the sidebar, `/scheduled`; `/settings/schedules` goes there).
- **"다시 확인".** The waiting task has "다시 확인" instead of "켜기"; it opens the same server card the AI's
  `schedule_create` raises (`scheduleCard(…, 'review')`: title on one line, schedule, the whole instruction, the
  addresses in it, long random-looking parts marked, the "allow" team connections) rendered by the chat's own
  `AskCard`, with "다시 켜기" (or with / without those connections) and "계속 멈춰 두기". Resuming is the
  confirmation: `confirmed_at`, `allowed_urls` = the card's addresses, `write_connections` = the picked connections,
  on from the next due time, audit `schedule.reconfirmed`. The answer is bound to the card's content (requestId = hash
  of the task, its addresses and the offered connections with their versions): a change in between is refused (409
  `schedule_card_changed`) and the card is shown again. Only the card's own answers count. An expired one-time task
  cannot be resumed (it says why). `GET/POST /api/schedules/:id/review`, own tasks only (404 otherwise).
- **Admins** see waiting tasks in Admin › Members ("확인을 기다리는 예약 작업", `GET /api/admin/schedule-reviews`):
  owner, schedule and since when, never the title or instruction (the person's own words, like their chats). Only the
  owner can confirm.
- Tests: `tests/unit/schedule-review.test.ts` (migration on existing rows, the run-time rule, switch refused, queue
  recovery, the card in two languages, keep / stale / typed answer / other person, resume and its run's addresses,
  connections changing under the card, expired, notices, admin list), the permission matrix, `web/test/e2e/
  exfil-followups.spec.ts`. Tests that need a task to run create it with the card's approval (`tests/lib/
  schedule-card.ts`).

## Allow a site for one conversation (feat/exfil-followups, 2026-10-30)

Review follow-up of the link budget: after 8 per answer / 30 per chat each new link asked one by one, where Claude Code
asks once per domain ("Yes, and don't ask again for this domain").

- **The choice.** An address card that is about where the address came from (not in the conversation, or over the link
  budget) offers "열기" (this address), "이 대화에서 이 사이트 허용 (<site>)" and "열지 않기". After the second, later
  addresses on the same site open without a card in that chat (`chat_allowed_sites`, migration 324, reader 1),
  outside the link budget (they spend none of it). The site is the registrable domain (eTLD+1) by the Public Suffix
  List with its private section, through `tldts` 7.0.30 (MIT, new server dependency; no network, the list is in the
  package): news.example.co.kr and example.co.kr are one site, alice.github.io and bob.github.io two,
  bucket.s3.amazonaws.com its own; a name that is itself a public suffix (co.kr, github.io), an IP address or a
  single-label name has no site and gets the plain two-answer card. IDN: compared in the URL's ASCII (punycode) form,
  shown with the Unicode form next to it.
- **Never wider.** One chat, one person: the row has the chat and the person who picked it, and counts only for that
  person in their own chat (another chat, another person, no person: none). Sub-agents of an answer use the turn's
  person and chat, so they share it both ways (a card a child's call raises offers the same choice). Scheduled runs
  start in a new chat, so they have none.
- **What it does not change.** `gateUrl` decides from the text and the database; the name is looked up only after
  it said yes, as before (an allowed site's names are looked up after the check, never before a card). A name that
  resolves into the office network is still refused after the lookup (web_fetch) or gets the office-network card
  (browser tools); private IP literals are refused before any card. An address with a long random-looking part
  (`opaqueParts` on the decoded address, so a Korean path is words) is never covered: it gets the card every time
  with that part highlighted (the plain address card now shows the address in a marked detail block when it has one).
  That card offers no site choice (review of feat/exfil-followups): it is the card an AI's first try to send data out
  raises, and one click there would trust the whole site for the rest of the chat; the next plain address of the site
  offers it.
  A query over 200 characters and every address while the office's exit address is unknown still ask, without the
  site choice. A confidential chat (Safe operations 1A) never offers it and ignores allowances made before.
- **A long name before the site** (review of feat/exfil-followups). `opaqueParts` cannot see data in a host name:
  names are lowercased (no mix of cases to tell a random label by), and dots or hyphens cut data into short pieces
  (`a1b2c3d4e5.f6a7b8c9d0.<site>`, letters only `qwhsjdkeuqpzmxnvbalskdjf.<site>`). A name also goes out in the
  clear to the name servers on the way, before any page opens, so data in it reaches more than the site. So an address
  whose part before the site is 20 characters or longer (`MAX_SITE_SUBDOMAIN`, dots and hyphens included) is never
  covered: its card highlights that part, with its own line ("사이트 이름 앞에 붙은 부분이 길어요"). Real sites rarely
  need that much (www, news, m.blog, docs, us-east-1.docs). An address with a user name or password is never covered
  either (the in-app browser takes one; web_fetch refuses it before the card).
- **Cost of the random-string rule.** Addresses with long ids (a git commit, a document id) on an allowed site still
  ask each time. Accepted: that is what such a part looks like when it carries data.
- **What it does not stop.** Allowing a site trusts whoever runs it: within these rules the AI can still send it
  readable text (words in a path, a short name before the site, many requests). The random-string and name rules stop
  bulk encodings, not a determined AI. That is the trust the person gives by picking the site (the card names it), as
  with Claude Code's domain allow; a confidential chat never has it.
- **The list.** `tldts` carries the Public Suffix List (MPL-2.0) compiled into the package and releases with its
  updates (about weekly; 7.0.30 is from 2026-05-02). A new suffix the pinned copy lacks only makes a site wider than it
  should be (a hosting platform's customers counted as one site), never opens anything the person did not pick; bump it
  with the other dependencies. Chosen over a vendored snapshot: the same pinned bytes and lockfile hash, plus the
  wildcard / exception / private-section rules and their tests upstream.
- Tests: `tests/unit/site-allow.test.ts` (suffix table with co.kr, go.kr, github.io, s3, blogspot, kawasaki.jp
  wildcards, IDN, IP, single label, trailing dot; card options; scope by chat and person; random-looking parts, long
  names before the site however cut, user name or password, long query, unknown exit address; outside the budget;
  confidential chat; DNS stub: no lookup before the decision, office answer refused after it, private literal before
  any card; a sub-agent opening the site without a card), `p0-exfil-server.test.ts` (adjusted to the choice card),
  `web/test/e2e/exfil-followups.spec.ts`.

## Exit address on every install (fix/pre-0212, 2026-10-30)

The 0.2.12 pre-release QA (plans/qa-real-2026-10-30, B1) found that a server without a relay — qa-test, Linux behind a
Cloudflare tunnel, as INSTALL-LINUX's public-address path; likely hosted servers too — never knew its public exit
address. Every `web_fetch` then asked with an "office public address" card (also for addresses the person typed, so the
link budget never applied), and the AI schedule card promised "opens without asking on each run" while every run was
refused. The founder left it to us; decision: keep the protection, make every install learn the address.

- **What the rule protects against.** web_fetch runs as the server account, outside the engine firewall. A page the AI
  fetched sees the address our request came from and can link to it; a fetch of that address goes out and comes back
  through the router or NAT in front of the server (hairpin NAT): an office router's admin page, a NAS or camera behind
  a port forward, or what a cloud host answers on its own public address. Private, local and on-link addresses were
  already refused by the address rules; the exit address is a public one, so it has to be known to be refused. While
  unknown, every address needs a person (`url-gate.ts` `noEgress`). Office installs learned it only from the relay's
  handshake (`AuthOk.seenIp`, the control connection's CF-Connecting-IP).
- **How every install learns it now (`tools/egress.ts`).** At start and every 30 minutes (±10 %), the server asks the
  release feed's new `GET /ip` (`scripts/release/worker.js`: the caller's `CF-Connecting-IP`, or `CF-Connecting-IPv6`
  when the first is Cloudflare's pseudo-IPv4 240.0.0.0/4, as plain text, `no-store`, no CORS), once over IPv4 and once over IPv6, the way web_fetch's own requests leave: the system
  resolver, the feed's address checked by web_fetch's rules, a raw socket pinned to it (`pinnedRequest`, no proxy from
  the environment), TLS to the feed's name. The answer must be one public address (64 bytes at most). Learned
  addresses join the relay's in the list web_fetch and connected services refuse on every hop (8 kept; an old one stays
  refused). The address itself is not logged. Production and office mode only (`main.ts`; dev learns it from its local
  relay, `bun test` never starts it).
- **"Known"** = since this start, the relay reported an address, or the feed told the IPv4 one, or the IPv6 one while the
  machine has no IPv4: no IPv4 address of its own, EAFNOSUPPORT, or ENETUNREACH / EADDRNOTAVAIL while the routing table
  has no IPv4 default route (Linux `/proc/net/route`; elsewhere, or unreadable, these count as a failed round). A router's
  or firewall's ICMP "network unreachable / prohibited" for the feed's IPv4 address — or a forged one — gives the same
  ENETUNREACH while every other IPv4 site opens through the NAT'd address (review of this change). IPv6 alone is not
  enough on a machine with IPv4: that one is the NAT'd one. An answer of the other family than asked is refused but
  counts for neither. While IPv4 is not known the server asks again after 1, 2, 5, 10, then every 30 minutes.
- **Fail-safe when unknown, as before.** No internet, the feed blocked, an older feed Worker (404), or
  `MYCEL_EXIT_ADDRESS_CHECK=off`: every web address asks, unattended runs open none. Hosted servers may reach the feed
  already (HWP plugin downloads; the tenant chain blocks only private ranges), self-installs need outbound https to it
  (INSTALL-LINUX). Right after a start, web_fetch and the schedule card wait for the first round (at most 6 s) instead of
  asking at once. The card wording no longer names an office ("its own public address", 해요체). Admin › System ›
  Diagnostics shows "Public address of the server" (QA 0.2.12 N5, `exit_address`, installed servers and office Macs):
  known (IPv4 / IPv6, or reported by the relay; ok), not known (warn: every web address asks and scheduled tasks open
  none, and the feed address it asks), or turned off by `MYCEL_EXIT_ADDRESS_CHECK=off` (warn, the same consequence).
  Never the address itself; the hosted cloud points at support instead of the network.
- **Unattended runs say why.** A scheduled run's person is marked `unattended`: the gate raises no card (it could only
  go unanswered) and tells the AI "nobody can confirm it here" — while the exit address is unknown, with the reason and
  that writing the address into the task changes nothing (QA: the AI told the person to do exactly that); for an address
  with a long query (always a card), that reason instead of "did not appear in the conversation".
- **Schedule cards say what a run will do here.** `scheduleCard(…, { urlsOpen })` (create and "다시 확인"): while the
  address is unknown the card says runs cannot open its addresses yet, and why, and its list is "addresses in the
  instruction"; the AI's result says so too. The addresses are still stored as the card showed them, so runs open them
  once the server knows its address. The review card's request id covers the task, not the wording, so a change of
  state between showing and answering does not void the answer. One address is said in the singular in English and
  Spanish ("the address below"; before, "the 1 addresses"). An address in the instruction with a query over 200
  characters always needs a person, so runs never open it: the card (create and "다시 확인") lists such addresses apart
  ("Addresses runs never open (long query)", the query highlighted) with a line that says so, the promise line counts
  only the others, and the AI's result says it too (feat/small-batch-1031). They are still stored with the task, as
  before; the gate's rule does not change.
- **Limits.** A server whose requests leave from more than one address (several uplinks, per-destination policy
  routing) learns the one its requests to the feed use, like the relay. A changed office address is refused from the
  next round on (≤ 30 minutes; the relay reconnects at once). The feed sees each server's address every 30 minutes (it
  sees it on update checks too); `MYCEL_EXIT_ADDRESS_CHECK=off` opts out. The answer is trusted like the relay's
  seenIp (our own infrastructure, over TLS to its name), not signed like updates: a wrong answer from a compromised
  feed would lose this one check only (private, local and on-link addresses stay refused, and the card rules apply).
  DNS tricks or a captive portal cannot answer (the certificate must name the feed; Bun's own CA list); `HTTPS_PROXY`
  is ignored like web_fetch ignores it. A TLS-intercepting proxy the operator made the server trust
  (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`) is learned as the address https leaves from, which is what pages fetched over https see; plain
  http that bypasses such a proxy leaves from an address the server does not learn (the feed redirects http to https,
  so it cannot be asked over http). Learned addresses add to the list, they never replace the relay's (the 8 most recent
  distinct ones are kept).
- **Deploy.** The feed Worker must be redeployed once (`bun scripts/release/hosting.ts setup`); until then `/ip` is 404
  and servers keep asking, as in 0.2.11. The change is one new path; every other path answers as before.
- Also in this change (same QA): step labels in five languages for `hwp_render`, `search`, the schedule and Drive tools
  and `generate_video` (raw names before); a Stop that ends an answer while it streams logs the same info line as one
  that ends a waiting request (Codex and Claude; before, nothing); the log shows token *counts* (a finite number under a
  plural "…tokens" key) instead of `[redacted]` — the redactor matches "token" in key names, a credential is never a
  number, and `token`, `accessToken` or any non-number stay redacted.
- Tests: `tests/unit/egress-learn.test.ts` (a fake feed on loopback over IPv4 and IPv6, stubbed lookups and interfaces:
  both families, 404, garbage, private and swapped answers, no IPv4, no route, the learner's rounds, back-off and log
  lines, waiting for the first round, the gate and web_fetch before and after, unattended runs, both schedule cards in
  five languages), `feed-worker-ip.test.ts`, `step-labels-tools.test.ts`, `b-proxy-usage-stop.test.ts` (B3),
  `server-app.test.ts` (log counts).

## Codex web search (cached) through the model proxy (feat/small-batch-1030, 2026-10-30)

QA 2026-10-30 B2: managed Codex (the team's AI connections) had no web search tool at all, so "Codex web search uses
its cached index" had nothing to apply to; asked to search, Codex guessed an address and used web_fetch. Founder:
Trina should feel like Claude Code, which has WebSearch.

- **Why.** Read from the pinned Codex 0.163.0 (and 0.164.0) with a recording fake upstream (no internet): with a
  custom model provider ("teamax", not "OpenAI": the name switches other OpenAI-only behaviour on, such as zstd
  request bodies) Codex offers no web search unless the provider says
  `supports_standalone_web_search`. The features list, the catalog's `supports_search_tool` (tool search, not web
  search) and `web_search="cached"` were not the cause. Codex 0.163 does not send the hosted `web_search` tool at
  all (nor with the built-in provider): with the flag the model gets a `web` namespace with one function, `run`
  (search_query, image_query, open,
  click, find, screenshot, finance, weather, sports, time), and **Codex runs each call itself** as
  `POST <base_url>/alpha/search` with the conversation, the call's commands and
  `settings: { allowed_callers: ["direct"], external_web_access: false }` (true only with `web_search="live"`). The
  answer is `{ "output": "<text for the model>" }`. `web_search="disabled"` removes the tool even with the flag.
- **Launch.** `engine/codex.ts` adds `-c model_providers.teamax.supports_standalone_web_search=true` to a managed
  turn whose search is on: the same rule as Claude's WebSearch (`!templateScope && !confidentialChat`: never in an
  approved template run or a confidential chat). Agent-own and dev turns use the built-in provider, which already has
  it, and are not changed.
- **Proxy.** `/codex/<chatgpt|openai>/alpha/search` goes to the same upstream with the connection's real credential
  (the same headers, refresh, 429 and budget handling as `/responses`). `checkSearchRequest`: a catalog model, only
  the keys, commands and settings this Codex sends (anything else 403, audited), inline content only, and
  `settings.external_web_access` written false whatever the engine sent. Refused in a confidential conversation and
  for a turn started without search (the Codex proxy token now carries the turn's tool policy; a token from before has
  search, as before). `externalSearch` also sees the `web` namespace and calls of it, so a `/responses` request that
  offers or replays the tool is refused in those turns too. One search counts as one request and one web search call
  (priced like the web_search tool for an API key; tokens when the answer gives them).
