- **What "cached" means here.** OpenAI answers from its own index and loads no page live for the call. The team
  server cannot see OpenAI's side: this is the same trust as the hosted tool's cached mode, and queries go to the model
  provider like Claude's WebSearch queries go to Anthropic.
- **No addresses through the search (review of feat/small-batch-1030).** The real Codex 0.164, run against a fake
  provider on 127.0.0.1, drops keys and settings the model adds (typed commands) but forwards `open` / `find` /
  `screenshot` / `click` with whatever `ref_id` the model wrote, including `https://<anything>`. What OpenAI's side
  does with an address it has not indexed (a later crawl, say) cannot be seen from here, so the proxy does not rely on
  it: a `ref_id` must be a reference to the search's own results (`turn0search0`, `turn0fetch3`: letters, digits, `_`,
  `-`); an address or a host is answered by the proxy itself (200, nothing upstream, `proxy.refused` audited) with a
  note telling the model to use `web_fetch`, which goes through the address card. This is Claude Code's split as well:
  WebSearch opens no page, WebFetch does. Commands hold Codex's shape (lists of at most 20 flat entries whose fields are
  text, numbers or lists of text; `response_length` a word): anything nested is 403. The step shows what was asked
  ("Web search: <query or address>").
- **A failed search fails alone.** A 401 or 429 from `/alpha/search` (a restricted API key without that scope, a
  search-only limit, `usage_not_included`) goes back to Codex as that search's failure and never marks the connection
  invalid / limited or starts a ChatGPT refresh; the model requests (`/responses`) keep deciding the connection's
  state. Codex never finishes the item of a failed search (the model gets "aborted"): the parser closes such a step as
  failed when the turn ends, instead of letting it look done. Search results are not "learned" addresses: Codex's answer is text, not
  structured hits, so a web_fetch of a result asks with the address card (Claude's structured hits open within the
  link budget).
- **Steps.** Codex starts the search item without its query and names it at the end; the step label is set then
  ("Web search: <query>"). While it runs it reads "Searching the web…". An open of one of the search's results
  (`turn0search0`) names no query (QA 2026-10-30 N1): it reads "Opening a search result". An open the proxy answered
  itself (an address) ends in Codex as done; the step shows it as failed with the reason ("Refused: a search opens only
  its own results …", N2). The proxy tells the turn what each search request asked for and which addresses it
  answered (ProxyTurnEvent `search`, as it answers and before Codex has the answer; only for an answer Codex ends an
  item with: a search refused for its shape, limited or failed upstream never completes its item, and its request
  would otherwise pair with the next item); the turn pairs each item that ended as done with one of those
  (`chat/codex-search-step.ts`: a refusal by the address the item names, only for refs that look like an address;
  else the oldest request of the same kind, an item whose action is an open or a find counting as an open even when
  it names its pattern; else the oldest one not refused, so none stays behind), and falls back to the item's own action (`open_page`, `find_in_page`) where no proxy is in
  the path. Review 2026-10-31: before, a find of a result ("'trixie'") left its request behind, and the next open
  without a query, a refused one included, took the wrong request (a refusal shown as done).
- Not verified here: the real `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/alpha/search` and `api.openai.com/v1/alpha/search`
  (tests never call OpenAI). Release gate: one real Codex search turn on an installed server (ChatGPT sign-in, and an
  API key if one is used). If the API-key upstream lacks the endpoint, Codex reports the search failed and goes on.
- Tests: `proxy-codex.test.ts` (forwarding, cached forced, refusals, confidential and no-search tokens, addresses
  answered locally, command shape, a refused / limited search leaving the connection alone),
  `codex-prod.test.ts` (fake Codex through the real launcher and proxy), `template-engine-lock.test.ts`,
  `engine.test.ts`, `safe-ops.test.ts`.

## Tool rounds per answer (feat/a9-followups, 2026-10-31)

- Claude Code's `--max-turns` for an answer is now the team setting `answerStepLimit` (Admin > Team settings, "한 답변의
  도구 사용 한도" / "Tool rounds per answer"), **default 150** (was a fixed 50), 10-500. Claude Code itself has no such
  cap, and the A9 comparison with Claude Code (2026-10-31, ten office tasks) showed Trina using many more
  tool calls than Claude Code with a shell (S17: 60 against 5) because it has no code execution yet.
- A round is one reply of the AI: the tools it calls together in one reply count once (`--max-turns` counts turns, not
  tool calls). A9's S17 made 60 calls in about 5 rounds, far from 50; a model that calls one tool per reply reaches
  the limit sooner, and that is what the higher default is for.
- Read when each answer starts (`ChatRuntime.maxEngineTurns`, once for all its attempts); a change applies to the next
  answer. A stored value that is not an integer in range reads as 150. The change is audited (`settings.update`).
- Unchanged: at the limit the answer pauses with "이어서 하기" ("Continue after the per-answer limit" above); the 20
  active minutes and 45 minutes in total; budgets (the model proxy stops a Claude answer as soon as a block budget is
  used up); each sub-agent keeps its own 50 rounds (`MAX_SUBAGENT_TURNS`), and children's rounds do not count for the
  main AI; the API engine keeps its own 30 rounds (it runs in the server and is not budget-checked per round, so it is
  not raised with this setting); Codex has no round cap, only the time limits. Scheduled tasks and approved template
  runs use the same answer limits (template runs also keep their fixed tool scope). The model proxy has no per-answer
  request count, and nothing else assumed 50.
- Cost: every round is one more model request with the conversation so far, so the limit is also how much one answer
  may spend before it pauses (150 is up to three times the old 50; "이어서 하기" starts another answer with the same
  limit). Budgets and the 20 / 45 minutes bound the spend; the setting's hint and for-admins say a higher limit can
  cost more (review 2026-10-31).
- Tests: `b-answer-step-limit.test.ts` (default 150 on the command line, admin change and audit, range and members
  refused, a bad stored value, the pause at the team limit, sub-agents at 50); the existing tool-limit tests in
  `b-chat.test.ts` and `b-subagents.test.ts` fix the limit through the runtime as before.

## Bulk edits in one call (feat/a9-followups, 2026-10-31)

- New turn tool **`edit_files`**: the same exact-string replacement (`old_string` → `new_string`, optional
  `replace_all`) in 1-50 text files at once (A9 S17: "change the status line in 30 notes" took 28 edit calls). The
  model streams each tool call; A9's edits came about 0.8 s apart and the server took about 20 ms each, so the time
  went into writing 28 calls, not into running them: one call with the paths and one replacement is shorter to write.
- **Each file is its own edit call.** The MCP handler (`mcp/protocol.ts` `editFiles`) runs every file through the same
  path as a separate `edit` call (`callTool`): the person loaded again, the approved-template scope, the skills/ card,
  the wider-audience card (once per folder, as for separate edits), read-before-write with the calling agent's own
  reads (a sub-agent's batch uses its reads), the version in the history, a conflict copy when someone changed the
  file since it was read, the per-turn limits, the file event and one `tool_events` row per file (tool `edit`, the
  batch call's id and sub-task), plus one `edit_files` row with the counts. A file that fails does not stop the
  others; the result lists every file (edited, or the reason). The call is an error only when no file was edited. Stop
  ends the batch before the next file, also with the API engine (its in-server handler gets the turn's stop signal like
  the gate's, review 2026-10-31: before, the files after a card went on being edited after Stop). Duplicate paths run
  once, also when spelled differently ("./a.md", "a//b.md", another case on a case-insensitive disk): an edit leaves
  the file read with its new content, so a second run applied a replacement whose new text holds the old one twice
  (review 2026-10-31). Paths are merged by their actual name only when the person may read the file (else as typed),
  so the merge tells nothing about hidden files. The batch's agent is looked up once and every file uses it.
- Not a seventh file tool: it is listed by the chat turn's tool set (so `--allowedTools`, Codex's enabled tools, the
  model proxy's tool list and general-purpose sub-agents have it; Explore does not), and the handler runs it only when
  the turn offers it. The remote MCP connector (Claude Code on a laptop has its own shell) and turns without a chat
  tool set do not have it. Confidential chats (Safe operations 1A) do not get it: they keep `edit`.
- Not done: a batch read. S17's 29 reads still take one call each (they already go out in one reply, so they do not
  use up rounds); a batch read needs a cap below Claude Code's MCP result limit (25,000 tokens by default) and its own image and PDF
  handling. The Python analysis box is the general answer to "many small changes".
- Instructions: with the tool, "To make the same exact change in many files, read them (several reads can go in one
  message), then change them all with one edit_files call."; always (A9 S17: answers left out the notes that were
  already as asked), "After changing many files or items, also list in your answer the ones you did not change: those
  already as asked, and those you skipped (with why)." Sub-agents' reports also say what they left unchanged and why.
- Step label: "여러 파일 수정 · <first path> +N" (five languages; the number is not translated).
- Tests: `b-edit-files.test.ts` (S17 shape with already-done, unread, no-access and duplicate files; all failing; bad
  input and the 50-file cap; conflict copy; wider-audience card once; a skills/ card per file; a sub-agent's own
  reads; confidential chats; the handler's per-file check, template refusal and Stop; one file under several
  spellings; label and instructions), `api-engine.test.ts` (Stop during a card with the API engine).

## One language in the answer (feat/small-batch-1031b, 2026-10-31)

- A9 S17 (plans/parity-eval-2026-10-30): three Korean answers began with English fragments ("Verify:", "Let me check
  the status lines…"), the text the model writes between tool calls. QA 0.2.12 B6 saw an English sentence in a Korean
  answer with sub-agents. The instructions already said `Answer in <locale language> unless the user writes in another
  language or asks otherwise.`; the model read the text between tool calls as outside the answer.
- One line right after it (`prompt.ts` `LANGUAGE_RULE`): "Write everything you say to the user in that language,
  including the short text between tool calls: no English narration such as "Let me check…" or "Verify:" when the
  answer is in another language." It names no language of its own ("that language" is the answer language above, so it
  follows the person's locale, the language they write in, or what they asked for) and asks nothing of an English
  answer. Its second sentence keeps content out of it (review): "Content the user asks for in another language (an
  email, a translation), code, file names and quotes stay as they are." An English email asked for in a Korean chat is
  written in English, with the words around it in Korean.
- Same place for every engine: the line is in the person lines (`personLines`), so the Claude system prompt, the
  Codex and API engine instructions and a resumed Claude session's `<turn_context>` all get it. It comes after the time
  line, which changes every minute, so the instructions before that line stay as they were.
- Sub-agents (`buildSubagentPrompt`, every definition gets it through `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file`) get
  `SUBAGENT_LANGUAGE_RULE` instead: their text never reaches the person, but the assistant passes parts of their report
  on, so the report is in that language unless the task names another.
- Tests: `b-chat.test.ts` (Claude, a resumed session, Codex, for a Korean user), `b-subagents.test.ts` (the sub-agents'
  instructions and the main AI's).

## Diagnostics: the relay line says what the server knows (feat/small-batch-1031b, 2026-10-31)

- Admin › System › Diagnostics said "No relay connection is set up, so the team can only connect from the office
  network" on every server without the relay, also on a Linux server behind a Cloudflare tunnel (`--public-host`) or an
  office Mac with its internet address, where the team connects from outside.
- `system/connection.ts` `publicAddress(cfg)`: `tunnel.host` (the Linux installer's `--public-host`, office mode's
  TEAMAX_PUBLIC_HOST), else the first `publicOrigins` entry (MYCEL_PUBLIC_ORIGINS, for example the server's own domain) that
  is https on the standard port with an internet name. localhost, IP addresses, local-network names (.local, .lan,
  .home.arpa, .internal …) and other ports (office mode lists the desks' `https://<mac>.local:8443` there) are not a
  public address. The server does not try the address: it says what is set up.
- A relay's team address is not a public address either (review): the hosted control plane lists the team's
  `https://<team>.trina.app` in `publicOrigins`, and that name goes to the relay, so a hosted server whose relay was not
  registered yet said "connect from outside without the relay". `isServiceHost` names are skipped, and so is this
  server's address at its relay when the relay client knows it (a self-relay's team address). `tunnel.host` stays as
  set: it is the owner's own statement of the public address. A trailing dot is dropped; reserved names (.test,
  .example, .invalid, .localdomain, .private, .arpa) are local too; an internationalized name stays in punycode, as
  `tunnel.host` is kept.
- The line: relay connected = its address (as before); no relay and a public address = ok, "A public address is set up
  (https://<host>), so the team can connect from outside without the relay."; office mode with one = the office
  wording plus the public address; neither = warn, "No relay or public address is set up, so the team can connect only
  from the office network." with where to turn on the relay, and on Linux the `--public-host` command. The hosted cloud
  keeps its support wording when neither is set up. Korean in 해요체; five languages.
- The Connection card says the same (review: it was the same wrong words): `GET /api/admin/connection` (owner only, as
  Diagnostics) carries `publicAddress` (host only, never a credential or path of an origin). Without the relay and with
  one, the mode is "Public address, no relay" (`system.mode.direct-public`) with a "Public address https://<host>" line
  and no "Off" badge, also in the change dialog's list and its confirmation; without one, "Office network only" and
  "Off" as before. The relay connecting / offline / replaced lines are unchanged.
- Tests: `g-linux-diag.test.ts` (each case on Linux and hosted, origins that do not count, a hosted team address and a
  self-relay's address, a connected relay, `publicAddress`), `office.test.ts` (office mode with and without its
  internet address), `g-routes.test.ts` (`publicAddress` in the connection status), `web/test/e2e/admin.spec.ts` (the
  Connection card with and without a public address).

## Drag rows onto a folder; text fields with a 3:1 edge (feat/files-drag-move, 2026-10-31)

- Founder request (2026-10-31): with four files selected in Files › Team folder, drag them onto a folder row
  ("company") to move them there, as in Google Drive or Finder. Before this, rows could be moved only with the row
  menu's or the selection bar's "Move", and dragging a file row only attached it to a chat's message box.
- What a drag takes (`lib/bulkFiles.ts` `dragSet`): the whole selection, as listed, when the row grabbed is selected;
  otherwise that row alone, and the selection stays as it was afterwards (`reportBatch(..., select = false)`). Folders
  can be dragged too.
- What it carries (`dragPayload`): `application/x-mycel-files-move` (the paths, JSON) when any of the items may be
  moved, and, for a file the AI may read, `TEAM_FILE_DRAG_TYPE` plus `text/plain` with that one file, as before, so
  the chat's message box still attaches it (it now sets `dropEffect = 'copy'`). A download-only file can be dragged to
  move it, and its drag carries no team file. A read-only file outside a movable selection drags into a chat only.
  The move type is accepted only where the drag started: the screen keeps the rows in a ref, and another tab's rows
  are not taken.
- Where it may land (`dropRefusal`): a folder row the person can write, and the breadcrumbs (moving up). Refused: the
  item itself (no hint), a dragged folder's own subfolder, a folder the person cannot write (read-only or
  navigation-only: "Can't move here"), the folder the items are already in, a drag with nothing movable, and any
  folder while a move is still running. A breadcrumb's access is asked with one `tree` call (`limit: 1`) per ancestor
  when a drag starts and remembered while the folder is open. Until the answer comes, the drop is allowed and the
  server decides per item, as for "Move".
- The drop runs the selection's "Move" (`moveItems`, shared with `bulkMove`): only items the person may change (the
  rest are skipped and counted in the toast), `moveMany` with one "hidden from other people" question for the batch,
  `onExists: 'rename'`, failures listed per item, and the same toast through the toast live region. The "Move" action
  stays the keyboard and screen reader path. Touch: no change.
- Targets handle `dragenter` as well as `dragover`. When the pointer enters a new element, Chromium decides the
  operation from `dragenter`, and `dragover` follows only with the next move (the e2e caught this: a breadcrumb
  showed nothing when the pointer entered it). A refused target still cancels the event, with `dropEffect = 'none'`,
  so a computer file dropped there does not fall through to the list's upload or to the browser, which would open
  the file in the app's tab. The trash view does the same for computer files. In the desktop app the window's
  `will-navigate` guard already stops a file:// navigation.
- While rows are dragged the breadcrumbs replace the selection bar, so the breadcrumbs can take a drop. The swap and
  the dimming of the dragged rows happen a tick after `dragstart`, because a DOM change inside `dragstart` can end
  the drag in Chromium. If a dragged row leaves the listing before `dragend` (a live update), the next pointer move
  with no button down ends the drag state. Several rows drag with an "N items" picture (`setDragImage`).
- Computer files dropped on a folder row the person can write are uploaded into that folder (`startUploads(list,
  folder)`), and the upload list shows the folder. A read-only folder row says "Can't upload here" and takes nothing.
- Text fields (design review): the input border was `--c-line` (#e9e3d8 on #ffffff, 1.28:1), shared with cards and
  dividers, so raising it would have made those heavy. A new token `--c-field-border` (Tailwind
  `border-field-border`) is for field edges only: `inputCls` (inputs, selects and text areas across the app), the
  chat message box, the edit-message and queued-message forms, the file panel's text editor, the Files search box
  and the sign-in language select. Values, against canvas / surface / subtle: Trina light #8c8378 (3.60 / 3.73 /
  3.34), Trina dark #776e64 (3.90 / 3.67 / 3.49), base light #8b8478 (3.52 / 3.70 / 3.28), base dark #7b766b
  (3.85 / 3.52 / 3.18). Focus was the old `--c-line-strong` border plus a 25% accent glow. The glow alone was about
  1.4:1, and the new rest border is close to `--c-line-strong`. Focus is now a 2px accent edge (`border-accent` +
  `ring-1 ring-accent`): Trina light 3.59 / 3.71 / 3.33, Trina dark 6.84 / 6.43 / 6.12, base light 6.02 / 6.34 /
  5.62, base dark 8.31 / 7.60 / 6.86. It is thicker and a different color from the rest border. `--c-line` is
  unchanged. `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` lists `--c-field-border` (tokens, contrast, the field and focus rules).
- Tests: `web/test/unit/bulk-files.test.ts` (drag set, payload types, every refusal and allowed target),
  `web/test/unit/field-contrast.test.ts` (both tokens ≥ 3:1 in all four looks, read from the CSS; `inputCls` uses
  them), `web/test/e2e/files.spec.ts` (two selected files dragged onto a folder; a row outside the selection; the
  selection dragged up onto a breadcrumb with the current one refused; read-only, navigation-only and self refused
  with nothing moved; computer files onto a folder row and a read-only one, also as a trusted drop of a file from
  disk through Chromium's drag input), `web/test/e2e/team-files.spec.ts` (a download-only file drags as a move only).
  Checked by hand in Electron 44 with the desktop app's web preferences and `will-navigate` rule: a selection
  dragged onto a folder moves; a file from disk dropped on a read-only folder row, on a folder row and on the sidebar
  uploads only on the folder row. That drag input does not take the browser's open-a-dropped-file path (a drop
  nobody takes did not navigate in plain Chromium either), so keeping a file out of the tab rests on the cancelled
  `dragenter` / `dragover` and on the window's `will-navigate` guard.
- Review (2026-10-31): a drop moves only the rows of a drag that started on this screen (the ref) and now also only
  when the drop carries that drag's own data, so a drag from another tab or app with the same type is not taken even
  if a drag from here was left without its `dragend`; e2e with a forged drag. The paths moved never come from the
  drop. Every move is checked by the server as before (`authorize` write on both paths, `intoItself`,
  `audience_narrowed`), so a refused target refuses there too. The edit-message and queued-message text areas sat
  inside a framed form and still drew `inputCls`'s new 1px accent ring (Tailwind emits `ring-1` after `ring-0`), a
  double edge on focus: they take `focus:ring-0!`. Not changed: a move (the "Move" action or a drop) that widens who
  can see an item does not ask; only one that hides it from people (into `users/<me>/`) does. Left for later.
- Composer focus (2026-10-31, as in Claude): the message box is focused most of the time, so the 2px
  accent edge was on screen nearly always, unlike Claude's quiet box. This commit keeps `--c-field-border` at rest
  and makes its focus a darker 1px edge (`focus-within:border-faint`, 5.55–5.82:1 on the surface, 1.5:1 against the
  rest edge) with no accent; every other field keeps the 2px accent edge.

## Old version folders (fix/prune-versions, 2026-11-01)

- **Problem.** On Linux servers and role-account Macs every update stages a whole version folder,
  `app/versions/<v>` (0.2.15: 484 MB of files, about 505 MB on disk; about 540 MB with the CJK fonts), and the
  installer adds `app/engines/<name>/<sha12>` for a new engine; nothing removed either. At one release a day that is
  about 16 GB a month, and a hosted Starter server (80 GB) fills within months. Office Macs were already bounded
  (`app`, `app.previous`, `app.failed`; staging and download removed after an update that worked).
- **Rule** (`server/src/system/prune.ts`, run by the server account: it owns `app/versions` and `app/engines`, so no
  root step). Kept: the target of `app/current`, the running version, `state.json` `current` and `previous` (Roll back;
  the bootstrap's way back when the current version does not verify, `native/cmd/mycel-bootstrap` `rollBack`), the
  newest staged version newer than current (`UpdateManager.status().available`), a version folder newer than current
  whose mtime or ctime is in the last 24 hours, and one not newer than current changed in the last hour (changed
  2026-11-10, below). Removed: every other folder directly under `app/versions` named like a version
  (`<n>.<n>.<n>[-+…]`; "notes" or "backup" stays), `.staging-*` and `*.partial` once a day old, and engine folders
  `current` no longer points to once both `current` and the folder are a day old. `lstat` only: a link is left (or,
  inside a removed folder, unlinked), never followed; `app/`, `app/versions`, `app/engines` and `<name>` must be real
  folders. Skipped while `state.json` has `pending`, or when `app/current` / `state.json` are missing or odd; checked
  again before each version folder is removed.
- **Why the 24-hour grace on version folders** (beyond the reviewer's rule): `mycel-ctl update` copies the new
  version to `<v>.partial`, renames it and only then runs `admin.js switch` (bun start plus a full verify, seconds),
  so for a moment the new folder is neither current nor previous; the installer's `older` bundle and a manual
  `stage-update` are switched to later by hand. A rename, chown or chmod moves ctime, and `cp -a` keeps the kit's
  mtime but not its ctime, so a just-copied folder always looks fresh. The cost is at most one extra version for a
  day.
- **One hour, not a day, for older versions** (fix/prune-old-versions-now, 2026-11-10). The dev test server updates
  about 40 times a day, so the 24-hour grace kept about 40 version folders (22 GB). The grace protects a folder that is
  about to be switched to. A folder newer than current can wait long for that (a scheduled `mycel-ctl update` waits for
  the team's update window), so it keeps the day. A folder not newer than current is switched to only by a roll-back:
  `admin.js switch <older>` and Admin's Roll back touch it and switch within seconds, and `mycel-ctl update --version
  <older>` copies or touches it and waits at most `--max-wait` (600 s) for running turns. One hour covers both. The
  check right before removal compares with the re-read `app/current`. An older kit that the installer only stages now
  goes at a run an hour later; to go back to it, run `mycel-ctl update --version <v>` or the installer again.
- **When.** 10 minutes after the server starts (the bootstrap's health check takes at most 120 s, `mycel-ctl update`
  waits 180 s), then hourly, under the operations lock (`OpsService.tryLock('prune')`: never during an update,
  backup, restore or export started from Admin). Not in office mode. `admin.js prune-versions [--dry-run]` runs it
  now; a real run is recorded in `data/prune-versions.json` for the Diagnostics line "Kept versions" (update group).
- **First run after 0.2.16.** Measured in a Debian 13 container (Colima, Apple M-series): 11 copies of the real 0.2.15
  bundle, 49,346 files, 5.2 GB; the dry run took 1.1 s, removing 9 versions (4.54 GB) 5.4 s; 1.01 GB kept. The removal
  is async with a yield every 500 entries, so the server keeps answering; on a slow disk it may take tens of seconds.
- **Engines are not referenced by versions.** The only reference is `app/engines/<name>/current` (and `server.json`
  `engine.claudeBin` / `codexBin` and the launcher's `--allow-cmd`, which name `current/<name>`); a version folder's
  `engines.lock.json` pins what the installer downloads, and for Codex its sha256 is the archive's, not the folder's.
  Only the installer changes engines (a version roll-back does not), so there is nothing a kept version would need.
- **Root files.** `mycel-ctl update` replaces root files in place (staged in `root/.new`, removed by `defer` and at the
  start of the next one) and keeps no old copies; `root/safe-ops` copies are renamed over. What could pile up was
  `.install-tmp/update-*` (download and unpacked bundle, about 600 MB) when `mycel-ctl update` was killed before its
  deferred `RemoveAll`: the next update now removes them first, under `root/.update.lock`, in the root-only folder.
  The hosted host's engine cache (`/var/cache/mycel-engines`) is the host's and is not touched.
- **No hard links between versions** (looked at, not done). Between 0.2.14 and 0.2.15, 424.7 of 484.0 MB (87.7 %) of
  the files are byte-identical at the same path, so linking unchanged files to `previous` would save about 425 MB per
  extra kept version. Not done: (1) hosted servers, the ones short on disk, update only through root's `mycel-ctl
  update`; root linking files from a folder the server account can write, and then `Lchown`-ing them, is exactly what
  `install-macos.sh` refuses ("a folder the server account could write may hold hard links to system files"); (2) in
  the server's own staging the extractor opens files with `O_TRUNC`, so links could only be made after verification,
  with a second full verification; (3) the kept versions would share inodes: one damaged file (a disk error, a stray
  write) would make both `current` and `previous` fail the bootstrap's check, and the automatic roll-back exists for
  exactly that. Version folders are never written after staging (the bootstrap refuses one whose files changed), so
  (3) is about damage, not normal use. With pruning the bound is 2–3 versions (1–1.5 GB) without it.
- **Go pinned to 1.27.3** in both workflows (`GO_VERSION`, `GOTOOLCHAIN: local`, the same as `versions.json`), not
  `go-version-file: native/go.mod` (`go 1.27` = whatever 1.27.x is newest that day): since the commit stamp left the Go
  programs (7952b040), their bytes change only with their code or the toolchain, and `needsRoot` should only follow the
  code. How to move it: `docs/RELEASE-CI.md` 3장 "Go 버전".
- **Office Macs.** Bounded as said; one gap closed: when releases fail several times in a row, each one's zip and
  unpacked bundle stayed in `update/download` and `update/staging` until an update worked. Now a new try removes those
  of other versions first (`office/update.ts` `install`).
- Tests: `tests/unit/g-prune.test.ts` (keep rule, dry run, pending and odd layouts skip, links, leftovers, a read-only
  folder, engines, an unremovable file, roll-back after a prune, the ops lock and office mode, the Diagnostics line),
  `tests/linux/prune-versions.ts` (Docker `debian:13`: four versions staged by `UpdateManager` and confirmed by the
  Linux bootstrap, `admin.js prune-versions` dry and real, the rule a day later next to root-owned leftovers and
  planted links, roll-back and the bootstrap's verify fallback after the prune), `native/cmd/mycel-ctl`
  `TestUpdateFromBundle` (an earlier update's `.install-tmp/update-*`), `tests/unit/office-update.test.ts` (two
  failed releases in a row), `tests/unit/release-ci.test.ts` (every `setup-go` uses the pin).
- **Review (2026-11-01), what changed before merge.**
  - *The hourly run collided with the automatic update.* Both were `setInterval(…, 1 h)` from the server's start, so
    they fired at the same moment: `autoUpdateTick` reads the feed (async), the prune takes the operations lock
    meanwhile (a run takes seconds even with nothing to remove: it measures the kept versions), and the update then
    found the lock busy, every hour, inside the update window too: Linux self-hosts would never update by themselves.
    The hourly prune now starts with the first run, 10 minutes after the start (`PRUNE_FIRST_MS`), so it ticks 10
    minutes off the update.
  - *Removal by path raced with whoever brings a folder in under the same name.* The first look and the removal were
    seconds apart (a slow disk: tens of seconds), and the removal walked paths: `mycel-ctl update --version <old>` or
    the installer (remove the old folder, copy a fresh one, rename it in) could have the fresh folder's files deleted
    from under it, then switch to a broken version (the bootstrap would roll back, but the update fails). Now each
    folder is looked at again right before (`app/current` and `state.json`, the version list for "available", the
    engine's `current`; still a day old by its ctime, owned by its parent folder's account: a root-owned leftover is
    reported as "remove it as root", not attempted), renamed to `.prune-<hex>` in the same folder (atomic) and only
    that name is removed. What keeps a fresh copy under the old name is its ctime of now: the same dev and inode as at
    the first look is checked too but proves little alone, since ext4 gives a freed inode number to the next folder
    made (measured in Docker: `rm -rf x; mkdir x` got the same number). A removal cut short leaves a `.prune-*` (not a version name, so never offered, staged or switched to),
    removed by a run a day later. A folder on another file system than its parent (a mount point named like a
    version) is never removed, and a removal stops at one inside. A file system that cannot rename the folder
    (`EXDEV`) falls back to removing it under its own name.
  - `admin.js prune-versions` refuses a real run as root (the record would be root's). The Diagnostics line names the
    folder that could not be removed.
  - Tests: `tests/unit/g-prune.test.ts` + 5 (a folder replaced before the second look, a folder brought in while the
    old one is removed, a switch and a pending update during the run, an engine's `current` moved during the run, the
    timer phase); the unremovable-file test now also checks that the leftover is no version and that a later run
    finishes it. `tests/linux/prune-versions.ts`: a tmpfs at `app/versions/0.8.0` (owned by the server account) stays,
    and no `.prune-*` is left.
- **Second review (2026-11-01).**
  - The unit test "a folder brought in again … before the second look" removed the old folder and made a new one; on
    ext4 (CI's ubuntu) the new folder got the old inode number, and with the test's clock two days ahead its ctime looked
    a day old, so it was removed. The test now moves the old folder aside (its inode stays taken); a second test makes
    the fresh folder with the old inode possible and shows what keeps it (ctime of now, written into the future for the
    test's clock). `g-prune.test.ts` passes 3/3 in Docker on an ext4 volume, as root and as uid 1000.
  - An automatic update no longer depends on the 10-minute offset: `OpsService.lockAfterPrune` waits for a prune that
    holds the lock (it keeps the prune's promise) and only then takes it; anything else holding it is logged ("another
    operation runs", with the holder) and tried again in an hour. Admin's buttons (backup, restore, export, update now)
    during a prune say "The server is removing old versions. Try again in a moment." (five languages) instead of the
    generic "another operation".
  - Mount points: a bind mount of the same file system has its parent's device, so the device check would have let the
    removal empty the mounted folder before `rmdir` failed. On Linux every run reads `/proc/self/mountinfo` (at the
    first look and again right before the rename) and leaves whole any folder at or above a mount point under `app/`
    ("holds a mount point: never removed"); elsewhere the device check stays. Docker: a tmpfs at
    `app/versions/0.7.0/web/data` leaves `0.7.0/server/main.js` in place (without mountinfo it was deleted).
  - A staged folder used again without a fresh copy is touched first, so its ctime is now and the prune leaves it:
    `UpdateManager.switchTo` (`lutimes`, before it verifies; Roll back and `admin.js switch <older>`) and `mycel-ctl
    update` when `app/versions/<v>` is already there and verifies (`UtimesNanoAt` with `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`; a root
    file change, and 0.2.16 needs the root update anyway). `TestUpdateFromBundle` checks it on the reuse path (same
    inode, mtime moved; it fails without the touch).
  - After the rename the `.prune-*` folder must still be the one looked at: same dev, inode and mtime, ctime not
    earlier. A rename keeps the mtime and moves the ctime forward (measured on overlayfs and ext4), so the ctime cannot
    be compared for equality. Otherwise it is renamed back and left, or, when the old name is taken meanwhile, kept as
    `.prune-*` with an error that says so.
  - A folder owned by another account is reported in a dry run too (before, the dry run listed it as removed); the
    owner compared is the parent folder's, so `admin.js prune-versions --dry-run` works as root and shows the same as
    the server account would. A leftover `.prune-*` under a day old says "renamed for removal in the last 24 hours".
- **Third review (2026-11-01).**
  - `autoUpdateTick` decides again once it holds the lock (the team's window, running answers, the hold rules): the
    first decision was made before waiting for a prune, and a long first prune could have taken the clock past the
    window, or answers could have started that the update would interrupt. When the second decision says no, the lock
    is given back and the reason returned (`outside_window`, `busy`, …) and logged.
  - A `.prune-*` folder that changed after the rename and whose old name was taken again meanwhile was left as
    `.prune-*` with "rename it back", but a run a day later would have removed it. It is now renamed to
    `.prune-hold-<hex>`, which no run removes and every run reports as an error (so Admin › System › Diagnostics keeps
    the warning until someone looks at it and renames or removes it); if even that rename fails, the message says that
    a run a day later removes it.
  - Tests: `g-prune.test.ts` + 2 (the decision made again after the wait: past the window and an answer started, each
    returns without updating and gives the lock back; it fails without the second decision; a held folder survives
    runs 4 and 30 days later and stays in the record's errors).

## AI reads video and audio (feat/video-read, 2026-10-31)

Founder: Trina should feel like Claude Code. A Claude Code user who gets a video runs ffmpeg for frames and whisper for
the words and reads both; Trina has no shell, so `read` does it on the server. Plan and review:
`plans/video-read-2026-10-31/` (outside this repository); where they disagreed, the review won.

- **`read` widened, no new tool.** Videos (mp4 m4v mov webm mkv avi 3gp) give frames (MCP image blocks, each after its
  time) and a timed transcript of the sound, in time order; audio files (mp3 m4a aac wav flac ogg oga opus weba amr aiff
  aif aifc caf wma) give the transcript (cover art is not a picture). The extensions live in `shared/src/media.ts`. New
  arguments, Claude Code style: `time` ("1:00-2:30", "90-150", "1:00-" to the end, "0:05" one moment; an end past the
  end stops there), `frames` (0-20; default one every 1.5 s, at most 12), `transcript: false`. They are refused on
  other files, like `pages`. Frames sit in the middle of equal parts of the window (never the black first frame) and
  are 1568 px for up to 4 frames, 1024 for up to 12, 768 above (the tool description says fewer frames give bigger
  pictures, for small text in screen recordings). A segment follows the frame whose part holds its start.
- **Limits of one result.** The 24,000-token rule of PDF reads: header and transcript first, then frames while they
  fit; the rest are named with the `time` and `frames` to send. The turn's 40 images / 10 MB are shared with every
  other read and sub-agent. A transcript too long for one result is cut at a segment and the rest named.
- **How much sound one read transcribes** (founder Q3): providers get at most 10 minutes per request; a read covers
  10 minutes next to frames and 30 minutes when no frames go (`frames: 0`, an audio file, or no pixels allowed), about
  9,000 Korean tokens. A 1-hour meeting is two reads; the result says what to send next. A long video without `time`
  gives 12 overview frames over the whole file and the first 10 minutes of transcript.
- **Linux servers only.** ffmpeg and ffprobe come from the distribution (`ffmpeg>=7:5.1` in `deps.txt`, installed by
  apt; never bundled: GPL and codec patents stay with the distribution; the installer stops without the package). A
  Mac server says it cannot read video yet (founder Q5: AVFoundation through `mycel-ocr` is phase 2). Without ffmpeg a
  Linux server says so. Nothing runs before these checks.
- **Converter safety** (`server/src/files/media.ts`). Every ffprobe / ffmpeg run is a converter run (bwrap, no network,
  read-only system, only the read's own work folder; the converter cgroup), `-threads 1`, with a time and memory limit
  (probe 15 s / 256 MiB, frame 20 s / 1 GiB, all frames 90 s, sound 90 s per piece / 512 MiB, packet scan 30 s), a cap
  on what each run may leave in the work folder (the input plus 64 MiB; plus the WAV for a sound run), and
  the allow-lists as input options: `-protocol_whitelist file`, demuxers `mov,matroska,avi,mp3,wav,flac,ogg,aac,amr,
  aiff,caf,asf`, and decoders by **decoder** name (ffmpeg checks those; must-fix of the review): h264 hevc vp8 vp9
  libdav1d mpeg4 mpeg1video mpeg2video mjpeg prores h263 png; aac mp3float mp3 mp2float mp2 ac3 eac3 opus vorbis flac
  alac amrnb amrwb wmav1 wmav2 and pcm_s16le/be, s24le/be, s32le/be, f32le/be, f64le/be, u8, s8, mulaw, alaw; text
  subtitles srt subrip ass ssa mov_text webvtt text (never decoded for a read). Checked on Debian 12 (ffmpeg 5.1.9) and
  13 (7.1.5) with a fixture per format: MP3 needs mp3float, AV1 libdav1d, MP2 audio `mp2` (not mp2float), WMA wmav2 in
  the asf demuxer; AMR-NB / AMR-WB decode with amrnb / amrwb. The format list refuses an HLS playlist or an ffconcat
  file named .mp4 (7.1 also refuses HLS with a non-standard extension itself).
  - ffprobe opens a decoder for **every** stream and refuses the whole file when one is not on the list (ffmpeg itself
    only warns for streams it does not map). So subtitle decoders and png (cover art) are on the list, and a file with
    a track no listed decoder opens (DTS, TrueHD, pcm_s64le …) is "this format cannot be read". The review's "first
    decodable audio stream" holds among listed decoders: the default one first, else the first.
  - `-show_entries … :stream_disposition=default,attached_pic:stream_side_data=rotation` (the disposition as a
    section; "stream=…,disposition" prints none). Only these fields are used: no title, comment or other tags, chapter
    names or subtitle text reach the AI.
  - Frames: `-ss` before `-i` (accurate seek), `scale='trunc(min(iw*sar,8192)/2)*2':ih,setsar=1` (square pixels),
    then the box, `format=rgb24`, PNG on **stdout**, then the Go normalizer (`mycel-safeops vision`) draws a new JPEG
    from pixels. ffmpeg's autorotate turns a 90° phone video portrait on 5.1 and 7.1. HDR (HLG / Dolby Vision HEVC
    10-bit) frames look washed out; tone mapping is later.
  - The WAV of a transcript piece is read back without following a link (`readOutput`, fix/converter-output-nofollow:
    a converter could leave a link to any file the server can read in its work folder). A run that replaced the work
    folder itself (`runIsolated` reports `killed: 'workdir'`; the macOS sandbox allows it, bwrap does not) is
    "damaged or unreadable", like the HWP renderer, never "too heavy": the whole read ends there, with no further frame
    or piece of sound, and nothing is read or removed under what was left in the folder's place. Files over 8192 px a
    side or 40 MP get no frames; files over 6 hours or 32 streams are refused.
- **Measured** (Debian containers, 4 arm64 cores, `-threads 1`): one 4K HEVC Main10 HLG frame peaks at 245-290 MB RSS
  (370-485 MB with ffmpeg's default threads), a 1080p H.264 frame at 65-90 MB, a frame 0.2-7.5 s; 12 frames of a 30 s
  1080p file with 10 s between keyframes took 12-14 s. Keyframe snapping for overviews is not built; the real 4 GB /
  2 vCPU box is a release check.
- **Binding the file.** The authorized path is opened with O_NOFOLLOW (regular, one link), its identity (device, inode,
  size, times) compared with the authorized one, copied into `<data>/work/vid-<uuid>/in.<ext>` (0700) in 4 MiB pieces
  off the event loop while it is hashed (a 1 GB copy does not freeze HTTP), compared again after the copy, and refused
  when the hash is download-only (quarantined). At most 1 GiB (founder Q2: a constant, not per plan; `readMaxMiB` is
  capped at 200 in the shared plan schema), with 2 GiB free left on the work folder's disk. Access, account and the
  file's identity are checked again right before delivery (`recheckSource`) and at socket drain; `readHashes` and
  `readPaths` get the file like any read (the transcript is file content for the wider-sharing check). At start every
  `vid-*` folder goes (no read survives a restart); a 10-minute memo keeps a file whose probe failed from running the
  converters again.
- **The media slot** (review should-fix). One media read at a time on the server (its own slot; voice input jobs keep
  theirs, and whisper.cpp itself is taken in turns with voice input first, below), a queue of 8, and up to 4 per person,
  so parallel sub-agents queue instead of failing "busy"; a wait over 5 minutes (20 s for a call without a chat turn) is
  "busy". Stop ends a read at once (the converters are killed, nothing more is sent).
- **The transcript** uses the team's speech provider (`speechProvider`), read when the read runs:
  - a new switch "Turn video sound into text" (`TeamSettings.aiMediaTranscripts`, founder Q1), separate from voice
    input, in its section. `null` = not chosen: `mediaTranscriptsDefault(provider, cpuCores)` in
    `shared/src/api/entities.ts` (the one place the default lives): on when the provider is this server and it has
    more than 2 CPU cores (`SMALL_SERVER_CORES`; real-server QA below), off on a smaller one and off for OpenRouter. An
    admin's choice always wins. A change of provider on save puts it back to `null`, so consent given for this server
    never sends sound to OpenRouter. Voice input off: no transcript.
  - OpenRouter: one request per piece through the voice input code (`sendToOpenRouter`: WAV, `zdr`, no data
    collection, the team model, fixed URL, no redirects, 60 s). Never from a confidential chat (`confidentialTurn`; the
    `read` tool is local, so the check is inside the transcript); a transcript already cached may be used there
    (review: nothing new leaves). No key: a note. OpenRouter's refusals (key, credits, 429, down) become the note.
  - This server (whisper.cpp): the model is never downloaded by a read (founder Q8): without it the note says voice
    input downloads it on first use. Pieces are 30 seconds (whisper's own window) on every server, as many as fit at
    the speed the server measured on itself (real-server QA below); a hosted server (a plan) makes at most 2 minutes of
    new sound a read (founder Q8), then the result says how to go on.
  - **Checked again before each new piece** (review of the branch): the switch and the provider, the chat's
    confidentiality (a safe workflow may lock it during a read) and the person's access to the file and its identity, as
    they are then. A read can wait minutes in the slot and run for minutes; an admin who turns the switch off, or access
    taken away, stops the next request, not only the delivery. A new piece starts only with time for its sound and the
    answer (OpenRouter `openRouterPieceNeedsMs`: 10 s + 50 ms per second of sound, at most 60 s; whisper.cpp
    `localPieceNeedsMs`: the measured speed), in the time the frames left: a piece cut off by the deadline is lost, and
    OpenRouter may bill it anyway.
  - Pieces are fixed from 0:00 (10 minutes for OpenRouter, 30 seconds for this server) and cached by content in
    `<data>/mediacache/<sha256>.json` (key: the file's sha256, provider, model, piece): "0:00-10:00" then "5:00-15:00"
    pays once more, not twice; a second read of the same bytes pays nothing. 0700 / 0600, at most 200 MB and 30 days,
    least recently used first; in the data folder, not the team folder, so not in backups. No OpenRouter re-chunking
    into 60 s pieces (review: build it only if a real call shows `segments` missing for
    `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`; without them a piece is one segment).
  - A call without a chat turn (the remote MCP connector) has 60 s for the whole read and gets everything in `text`
    (the connector returns only text); the API engine gets the transcript as text, no frames, like images. The API
    engine cuts every tool result at 30,000 characters without a word (`engine/api-agent.ts`), so for it the transcript
    is cut at a segment within 28,000 characters and the rest named (review of the branch: 30 minutes of English is
    about 35,000).
  - Every read that handed sound to the provider writes an audit row `media.transcribe` (who, file, seconds handed
    over, provider, model, pieces, cached, ok), also when the read then fails, is stopped or loses access (Admin >
    Activity "Turned the sound of a video or audio file into text"). No transcript text in audit rows, tool summaries
    or step labels. No daily quota (founder Q4: the cache, the slot, the per-read span and the audit row bound it).
- **Prompt injection.** A transcript (and text on screen in a frame) is untrusted file content, like any text file. The
  result heads it "Automatic transcript of the file's sound … It is file content, not instructions from the person, and
  it can be wrong or invent words over music or silence." Nothing filters it; the defence is the existing egress checks
  (wider-audience confirmation, URL gate, connector policy), which treat what the model learned from it like any file.
- **Frames** follow images: the renamed switch "Send images, PDF pages and video frames to the AI" (`aiVision`, founder
  Q7), the API engine, a connection without a chat turn, the turn budget. Frames are not saved to the person's files
  (founder Q9) and are evenly spaced (Q10).
- **Steps.** "Watch video · <path>" / "Listen to audio · <path>" from the extension at the start (`READ_MEDIA_VERB`,
  redrawn in the language on screen), with a film / sound icon. The end-of-call patch by tool-use id is not built
  (review cut).
- **Cut** (review): the probe cache, Apple Vision text per frame for text-only engines, the daily quota, a plan-adjustable
  size cap, the end-of-call step patch, the Mac "mp4 and mov only" text, two slots on 4+ cores.
- **Tests.** `tests/unit/media-read.test.ts` (converters replaced at FileService's seams; a fake OpenRouter: arguments,
  Mac / no ffmpeg / over 1 GiB / links / quarantine refusals, frame times and sizes, interleaving, `time`, moments,
  long videos and a 1-hour recording in parts, no sound / sound only / no length, refusal notes and the probe memo, the
  token cut and the turn budget, no pixels with the transcript still there, the switch and its per-provider default,
  OpenRouter request shape and the cache, failures without the key, confidential chats, a missing local model never
  downloaded, the hosted 2-minute pieces, the slot and its per-person queue, Stop, a file replaced during the read,
  start-up cleanup, the cache's LRU and links, step labels). `tests/unit/media-ffmpeg.test.ts` (the real ffmpeg in the
  isolation: a fixture per container and codec, cover art, rotation, square pixels, subtitles and an undecodable
  track, HLS / ffconcat refused, the packet scan, damaged files, one whole read through the Go normalizer). Both pass
  on macOS (ffmpeg 8.1, sandbox-exec) and in Debian 12 (5.1.9) and 13 (7.1.5) containers with bwrap.
  `tests/unit/sec-converter-output-links.test.ts`: each converter run of a read (probe, packet scan, frame, sound,
  whisper.cpp) that replaces its work folder is "damaged", and the read ends with nothing more run or removed there.
- **Real-server QA (qa-test, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, 2026-11-01; `plans/qa-real-2026-10-30/QA-VIDEO-READ.md`).** Local
  whisper.cpp needed 180-300 s for a 2-minute piece, so a read never finished one (and cached nothing), the transcript
  took the frames' time (0 of 12 frames after 308 s), and voice input slowed to 336 s next to it. What changed:
  - **Frames first.** A read makes its frames (at most 90 s), then the transcript in the time left, minus 5 s kept for
    the result (`RESULT_RESERVE_MS`); the converters of a piece (the sound cut, whisper.cpp, OpenRouter) get no more
    than that. Frames are counted against the turn's image budget when they are delivered, after the transcript. The
    "Not shown" line asks for `transcript: false`, so the suggested call for the frames left over does not wait for the
    sound again.
  - **Measured local pieces.** 30-second pieces (cache key per piece length, so the 2-minute ones of the QA build are
    simply not reused; OpenRouter keeps 10 minutes). The speed is seconds of whisper.cpp work per second of sound, kept
    for the server in the `settings` row `media.localSpeed` (per model and thread count), a moving average after every
    piece and every voice input job. Before measuring: 2.5 s a second (on the slow side). No single run may poison it
    (review of the branch: one 5.6 s dictation that took 300 s, or one read piece cut off at 200 s, made every later
    read plan no piece at all): a sample counts at most half or twice the value it meets, weighted by its length
    (0.3 for a 30 s piece, a sixth of that for a 5 s dictation); a clip under 10 s is never the first measurement; a
    run stopped by its time counts only when that is slower than the value; the value stays within 0.05-6 s a second
    (`LOCAL_SPEED_MAX`, also when read back); a piece with under 3 s above -50 dBFS (room tone, a hum: quick for
    whisper.cpp) is not measured. And a read whose measured speed lets no piece start still starts its
    first new piece when the time holds one at the default speed, so a wrong value is measured again and comes down.
    A piece costs at least a whole 30 s window, plus 5 s, times 1.2 (`localPieceNeedsMs`); a piece starts only when
    that fits in the time left, and the plan is checked again with the new speed before each piece. A piece stopped by
    the read's time is "time", not
    "failed": the note says how far the transcript got and that reading again goes on from there (the pieces made are
    kept), or, with none made, that reading again with `frames: 0` leaves more time.
  - **Threads.** whisper.cpp gets 2 threads on a 2-core box (one core less than the budget elsewhere, at most 4;
    `whisperThreads`), and its CPU-seconds limit is the time limit times its threads (`cgexecPrefix(timeoutMs,
    threads)`; RLIMIT_CPU counts all threads, so `-t 2` would have been stopped at half its time).
  - **No temperature fallback for a read's pieces** (`-nf`; review of the branch). whisper.cpp decodes odd sound again
    at higher temperatures, which made some short clips take 5 times as long. Measured before adopting it (Debian 13,
    2 CPUs, small, 2 threads): the QA's 5.6 s Korean clip 20.3 s instead of 72.5 s (both wrong, romanized); nine 30 s
    pieces of its Korean / English recording 281 s instead of 288 s, Korean CER 32.5 % instead of 32.7 %, English WER
    16.8 % instead of 15.0 % (one piece; the TTS numbers spelled out count as errors in both); a 6.8 s dictation the
    same text in 20 s. Voice input keeps the fallback (a person waits for those words, and nothing plans its time).
  - **Small servers.** On 2 cores or fewer (`cpuBudget`: the plan's cores, else the machine's), "Turn video sound into
    text" starts off; the read says why ("이 서버에서는 소리를 글로 바꾸는 데 오래 걸려서 꺼 두었어요. 관리자가 … 켤 수 있어요."),
    frames still go, and the settings switch says the same. `GET /api/admin/speech-host` gives the page the cores, the
    piece length, a hosted server's cap and the measured speed, so the switch's text follows the server (no "2 minutes
    per read" on a self-installed one).
  - **Voice input first** (`jobs/whisper-turns.ts`). One whisper.cpp at a time: a voice input job marks itself at
    once, stops a video piece that is running (it yields and is made again after, if the read's time allows) and runs
    alone; a video piece does not start while a dictation waits or runs, and the turn is taken in the same step that
    finds it free (review of the branch: a piece and a dictation that came in the same tick both ran). A piece waits
    for voice input at most 45 s (`PIECE_WAIT_MS`; an uploaded hour of recording is a voice input job too and must not
    hold the read and the server's one media slot for its whole time): then the read says voice input is using the
    transcription now and that reading again in a moment goes on. A run that finished as voice input came keeps its
    answer (whisperFile throws 'aborted' only for a run it killed). Chosen over a larger memory limit for
    whisper: one whisper.cpp small run is 767 MB RSS for a 30 s piece and 868 MB for 2 minutes (measured, Debian 13,
    2 CPUs), under the converter cgroup's `memory.high` of 821 MiB on a 4 GB box when alone, and two together do not fit
    any limit that box can give while also sharing its 2 vCPUs. A separate cgroup would also need a root-side change.
  - **Silence.** The WAV of a piece is checked before it is sent, in 100 ms frames: a frame is sound above -70 dBFS
    RMS, so only (near) digital silence counts as silence: recording gaps, padding, a muted track. Under 0.3 s of sound
    a piece is silence, cached as such, never sent. In a piece with at least 1 s of sound, lines whose time holds none
    are dropped (whisper invents them over silence). The first build used -50 dBFS (review of the branch): quiet speech
    that whisper small reads word for word (a recording peaking at -42 dBFS, mean -56) measured 0.0 s of sound, was
    cached as silence for 30 days, and next to one loud word two of its three lines were dropped; the cache key is
    `transcript-v2`, so nothing kept by that build is used. Room tone is sound now, and whisper.cpp decides there as
    before the change. Each piece keeps its language and the header names the languages by how long they are spoken
    (`transcriptLanguages`), never from a silent piece. A piece with under 8 s of sound runs on whisper's own guess
    first, since a told language can come back as a translation (measured: English told `ko` gave "이제 Friday에 입장해
    봅시다.", Korean told `en` an English sentence). Only when whisper.cpp is unsure (its own probability under 0.5, read
    from its log line, so a read's pieces run without `-np`) it runs again told the file's language, the one most spoken
    in pieces whose language counts (`Piece.sure`: 8 s of sound or more, or whisper sure), else the team's. That answer
    is kept (`acceptRetry`) when it is not whisper's "(speaking in foreign language)" caption (`saysOtherLanguage`) or
    one of its video-outro inventions ("구독과 좋아요를 눌러주세요!", "see you in the next video"), and is in the same writing
    system as the first (`writingSystem`: Hangul, Latin, kana/Han), or the first was in kana or Han and the told language
    is Korean or English; a retry that fails keeps the first answer (only Stop or a replaced work folder end the read). A language a retry proved is told to the read's next
    short pieces at once (an all-short file does not run every piece twice), and is dropped again for a piece that
    answers with the caption. A told language is never reported as heard (`Piece.hint`, cached as such), and an unsure
    guess never becomes the file's language for other pieces. The cache key is `transcript-v4`.
    - How the retry rule was chosen (Debian 13, 2 CPUs, small, `-nf`, `-ojf`): 16 `say` clips of 3-7 s (Korean,
      English, and Japanese and Chinese as controls, each clean and as a noisy phone copy) and 15 pieces of the QA's
      recordings (its short Korean files and 5 s windows of its Korean / English meeting), each run on whisper's own
      guess, told `ko` and told `en`, on a Korean and an English team (94 cases). Whisper was unsure (p < 0.5) only on
      the QA's Korean TTS pieces: ja at p 0.24-0.32 written in kana, or nothing at all; every English, Japanese and
      Chinese clip and every `say` Korean clip was sure (p 0.53-0.997), so no translation of a sure piece can happen.
      Correct answers (right writing system, no caption or invention), in production order: same writing system only
      (the previous rule) 81/94; whisper's mean token probability with a 0.05 margin 81/94 (it does not separate the
      cases: its kana inventions scored 0.45-0.59, the Hangul retries 0.45-0.52); the kana/Han rule 83/94, and with
      the invention filter the same 83/94 with three fewer invented sentences kept. Told every language regardless of
      p (a stress test), the kana/Han rule would take Hangul for real Japanese and Chinese speakers (77-78/94): it only
      holds because those are never unsure. On an English team a short Korean piece whisper is unsure of stays poor
      (romanized or nothing), but it is never labelled `en` or replaced by an invention.
    - History: the first build told every short piece the team's language (real-server re-check N1: qa-test's team is
      English, so short Korean sentences came out as romanized nonsense labelled `en`); the next one told it the file's
      language up front and counted unsure guesses as heard (re-review of b5e89a8c). Longer pieces are always detected,
      so an English video in a Korean team stays English.
  - **The window** keeps a sentence that began just before it (`end > from && start < to`).
  - **Settings form.** Picking another provider in the form shows that provider's default; picking the saved one
    again brings the saved choice back. Only a save that changes the provider resets it (`transcriptsAfterProvider`).
  - **Failure notes** name whisper.cpp's reason once ("받아쓰기에 실패했어요(memory)."; before, the Korean message was
    put inside itself). The image, video and voice input notes are 해요체 like the rest (`vision-text.ts`,
    `openrouter-stt.ts`, `transcribe.ts`); nothing saved is matched by their older wording.
  - The installer no longer warns that ffmpeg is missing: `deps.txt` already stops an install without the package.
  - Measured in a Debian 13 container limited to 2 CPUs and 4 GB (Apple Silicon host, arm64 whisper.cpp 1.9.5 built
    like the kit, small model, the QA's recording): a 30 s piece of speech 34-36 s with 2 threads and 62-95 s with 1;
    a 2-minute piece 87 s with 2 threads and 154 s with 1; 30 s of silence 18 s (and it made up a word). Each run spends
    about 8 s of encoder time on detecting the language and often a third pass on the last second or two of a piece.
    The x86 QA box is slower (226 s / 179 s for 2 minutes): QA times it again there.
- **Release checks** (people, on an installed Linux server): a real Claude Code and a real Codex turn reading a video;
  a real iPhone HEVC file on a 4 GB / 2 vCPU box (memory, the 90 s frame budget); a 1-hour meeting recording in two
  reads; an mp3 with cover art; a confidential chat with OpenRouter (no request); one real OpenRouter call to see
  whether `segments` (timestamps) come back for `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`.

## Search by meaning off by default (feat/semantic-default-off, 2026-11-01)

CEO decision: the `search` tool is off unless `MYCEL_SEMANTIC=on` (before: on unless `off`). Trina is built for team
folders, and a team folder has many files; there the tool did more harm than good.

- **Measured** (Apple M1 Pro, main `91cc66c9`, the real `SemanticIndex` and `localEmbedder`, no thread limit). 28
  questions worded without the documents' words (document "자녀 돌잔치 10만 원", question "아이 첫 생일 축하금 줘?").
  - 35 files of a made-up 12-person office: the right file among the 8 passages the AI gets for 26/28, first for 19/28.
  - The same 35 plus about 2,900 internal planning text files (16,292 chunks): among the 8 for 16/28, first for 11/28.
    Scores bunch at 0.83–0.88, so review reports and test expense CSVs came ahead of the right document.
  - Indexing 26 chunks/s on about 3.6 cores (10 min 24 s for the 16,292 chunks; with the background schedule, 1 minute
    every 5, about 55 minutes on that Mac, slower on a 2-core Linux server). Peak memory about 1.9 GB (390 MB on the
    small folder; the 150–300 MB above is the model alone). Whether that is ONNX's arena growing to the largest batch
    or a leak was not checked.
  - Query 7–13 ms. A Korean question did not find an English contract. CP949 CSVs (Korean Excel's default) are
    indexed as mojibake: `SemanticIndex.textOf` decodes plain text as UTF-8 only, while grep reads CP949.
  - ripgrep on the large folder: 0.1–0.5 s, and it found two of the misses directly (`위약|late delivery`, the agency name).
- **Off means**: the tool is not registered, so the prompts do not mention it (`chat/prompt.ts` checks the tool list),
  nothing is indexed in the background and the model is neither downloaded nor loaded. An existing `<data>/semantic.db`
  and `<data>/models/Xenova/multilingual-e5-small` stay on disk and are used again with `on`; nothing deletes them.
  Bundles still carry the runtime (`scripts/vendor-semantic.ts`), so `on` needs no other build.
- **Before turning it on by default again**: CP949 like grep, the file name and heading in each chunk, a keyword
  score mixed in, and memory while indexing; then the same test on a folder of thousands of files.
- Tests: the tool lists in `c-tools` and `i-wiring` have no `search`; `g-semantic-lazy`: only `on` turns it on.

## Skills: the whole list, the skill tool (Plan A, 2026-11-01)

The AI knew a skill only from the instructions' `## Team skills` list, cut at 50 entries without a word (personal
skills first, then team skills by name): a team with plugin skills or many folders lost the rest, though "/name"
still worked. Each line also carried the path and the whole description (up to 1,024 characters). This works like
Claude Code's skill listing now (read from Claude Code 2.1.312; the repo pins 2.1.305, which looks the same):

1. **Every skill is one line**: `- name [personal]: description`, the description on one line and cut at 160
   characters, no path (a name two skills share gets its path). The lines have a fixed budget of 8,000 characters
   (`SKILL_LIST_BUDGET`; Claude Code: 1% of a 200K context x 4 characters). Over it every name stays and descriptions
   go first to the person's own skills, then by usage (each use counts 0.5^(days/7); other people's uses of a skill
   the person can read count a quarter, a tie-break for new members), then by name. When even the names do not fit,
   the most important ones stay and the last line says how many more there are. The budget is not a team setting.
2. **The order is fixed for a chat** (`chat_skill_lists.ranked`, migration 217): computed at its first turn, so the
   instructions stay the same from turn to turn and the engines' prompt cache holds (Codex and the API engine build
   them every turn). A skill added later comes after the fixed ones.
3. **Two tools, for all three engines and the sub-agents** (general-purpose and Explore): `skill(name)` loads the
   full text, like Claude Code's Skill tool, as a `<team_skill>` block with the same rules as "/name" (resource base,
   no scripts, allowed-tools grants nothing); `find_skills(query)` matches words in names, descriptions and folders
   (Korean in two-letter pieces, so particles do not matter; English words with a simple plural), plus usage and a
   little for a skill whose folders share a word with the chat's project folder; top 10. Both walk the skills of the
   person as they are now on every call (`listSkills`, then `readSkill` through `authorize`), so a skill in a folder
   they cannot read is never named, found or loaded, by the main AI or a sub-agent; a personal skill only for its
   owner. A loaded skill counts as a use (team skills only, as before), joins the chat's read scope like "/name" and
   counts as outside content like a read of its file. Reading a skill's file by path still works. They are in the
   turn's tool list, so the model proxy's exact names for the turn, `--allowedTools` and Codex's `enabled_tools`
   carry them. Claude Code's own `Skill` and `ToolSearch` stay denied (they read `.claude/skills` from disk, past the
   folder permissions, and Codex and the API engine have nothing like them); Codex's skills stay off. Confidential
   chats keep them (they read only team files). A scheduled template run refuses them like any non-file tool.
4. **When the list is cut**, the server puts up to 3 skills whose words clearly match the message in a
   `<skill_hints>` block in front of it (not for "/name"). The instructions stay as they were, so the cache holds.
5. **A resumed Claude session** keeps the instructions it started with. Fresh instructions record what they listed
   (`chat_skill_lists.listed`: path, name and a hash of name, description and text, with the session id); a resumed
   turn's `<turn_context>` says which skills were added, changed or removed since then (at most 2,000 characters).
   A session whose start was not recorded (older, or another session) is told its list may be out of date. Codex and
   the API engine start fresh every turn, so their list is always current and needs no note.
6. **Caps are said, not silent.** The walk reads 1,000 entries per skills root (was 200); over it, skill managers
   (and the owner of a personal skills folder) see a skill issue `too_many`. A scan reads each folder's listing once
   (`authorize`'s `dirs` memo: made by one synchronous walk for one person and dropped with it, never passed to a
   write, and it only says which names a folder had: every step is still lstat'ed and realpath-checked and access is
   decided on the names found on disk), so 1,000 skills in one folder take about 0.2 s instead of 2 s. Team rules stay the first 10 by file name; the instructions
   name how many more were left out and skill managers see `too_many_rules`. The Team skills page says, only when
   something is left out, "skills 120 · in the AI's list with their description 64 · by name only 56" and how many
   rule files the AI follows (`SkillsOverview.aiList`).
7. **External-service tools: shown, not lifted** (founder, 2026-11-01; lifted since by "Connection tools: deferred,
   found and called" below). The caps stay 100 tools per MCP connection
   and 200 per answer, and there is no `find_tools` / `call_tool`. A check counts every tool the service lists
   (`integrations.tools_total`, migration 327): Settings > External services says "100 of 150 tools", and the AI's
   instructions say how many of a connection's tools it has when either cap left some out. The order of connections
   is unchanged (by name), so the tool list stays the same from turn to turn.

This replaces the 50-entry index in "Skills: folder permissions and personal skills" above; the rest of that entry
stands.
## OpenRouter speech: the language of long pieces, quiet sound, FLAC, DeepInfra (feat/stt-openrouter-tune, 2026-11-01)

The STT test for the hosted plan (OpenRouter `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, DeepInfra US, $0.012 an hour; plans
`stt-hosted-2026-11-01`) found four things to change in the request voice input and video / audio reads share
(`jobs/openrouter-stt.ts`, `jobs/speech-language.ts`, `files/service.ts` mediaTranscript). Everything was measured again
on its clips (macOS `say` meetings, the QA's 13-minute recording) through the real read path and the real voice input
path with the real ffmpeg and OpenRouter, and the rule was also applied to every recorded answer pair
(`tests/fixtures/stt`, `tests/unit/speech-language.test.ts`; the tests never call OpenRouter).

- **The language of a long piece.** whisper names one language for a whole request from its first 30 seconds and
  writes everything in it: the QA meeting's first 10 minutes were heard as Japanese and came back translated
  (Hangul CER 97.7%). A piece (or a voice recording) of 60 s or more is still sent without a language first. It is sent
  once more, told the file's language (the one most heard in its other pieces) or else the team's
  (`longRetryLanguage`), when that is not what whisper heard and: what it heard is neither the team's language nor
  English, or whisper was unsure of its words (mean `avg_logprob` under -0.4: its transcripts measured -0.04 to -0.36,
  its translations into a wrong language -0.48 to -2.3), or another piece of the file was heard in another language.
  The answer kept (`keepLongRetry`) is the one whisper is surer of: the retry wins only when it is not the "(foreign
  language)" caption, at least a quarter of its speech time is in the told language's script (Japanese told `ko` stayed
  Japanese), and its confidence is higher by 0.1 or more, where both are counted over the longer of the two answers and
  time an answer left out counts as -1 (told `ko`, the QA meeting's English last part dropped 55 s of English and would
  otherwise have won). A told language is never reported as heard (`Piece.hint` as before, `language: null` for voice
  input). A retry that fails keeps the first answer; it starts only with time for it, and a confidential chat sends
  nothing, retry included. In a read the retry goes only after the same checks as a new piece (the switch, the
  provider, a confidential lock, the person's access to the file), since the first answer can take a minute; switched
  off or locked meanwhile, the first answer stays (review of the branch). The sound is packed once for both requests.
  Short pieces keep the earlier rules.
  - Measured on DeepInfra answers: QA meeting (Korean team) Hangul CER 97.7% -> 20.3%, English WER 59% -> 28%, timestamps
    of its lines within 0.16 s (were 4.3 s off); as one 13-minute voice recording Hangul 8.1%, English 37%. A Japanese
    meeting stays Japanese (checked, told `ko`, kept). 10 minutes of Korean, a Korean-English meeting, English on a
    Korean team: not checked. Of the QA meeting's 27 half-minute pieces as recorded both ways, the answer kept is in the
    language mostly spoken in 26 (the 27th was heard as Korean, the team's language, with 16 s English and 12 s Korean).
  - Not chosen: always telling long pieces the team's language (English sections lost a 30 s window each: English WER
    36%, and a Japanese file would be forced into Korean); 30-second pieces each detected (`fr`, `ja`, `es` came back for
    Korean, Hangul CER 51%). A per-window merge of the two answers (each 30 s from the one whisper is surer of)
    measured Hangul 7.7% and English WER 23.5% on the WAV answers, but can drop or repeat a line at each switch; not
    built.
- **Language names.** Groq answers `"Korean"` / `"English"`, DeepInfra `ko` / `en`: the answer's language is read as
  whisper's code (`languageCode`, whisper's own list of names and aliases); a name it does not know counts as none.
- **Quiet sound** is raised before it is sent (`quietGainDb`): when the speech level (95th percentile of the RMS of
  100 ms frames with sound) is under -40 dBFS it is raised to -40, by 20 dB at most, never past -1 dBFS for the loudest
  0.1% of samples; louder sound is untouched. A room microphone peaking at -45 dBFS: 10.2% CER -> 0.6%. Room tone with
  no speech stayed without words up to +20 dB and became "Thank you." from +30 dB, and so did ffmpeg's `loudnorm`
  (I=-20), which also took 14 s for 10 minutes on one thread (it works at 192 kHz): not used.
- **FLAC, not MP3.** The sound goes as 16 kHz mono FLAC (ffmpeg's own encoder, in the converter isolation with only the
  WAV demuxer and PCM decoder, no tags, read back without following a link, a fresh name for every piece). It is
  lossless, so the answers are the WAV's (same words and `avg_logprob`), at 38-49% of the size (10 minutes: 7.1-9.5 MB
  instead of 19.2 MB). MP3 at 48, 64 and 96 kbps and 32 kbps Opus all changed what whisper wrote on the two-minute
  Korean-English meeting (an English line came back translated into Korean: 5.4% CER as WAV or FLAC, 13.6-22.6% lossy;
  DeepInfra gave the same answer every time). 10 minutes from this Mac on a good line: WAV 7.5-11.9 s, FLAC 7.7-8.2 s,
  MP3 4.8-5.0 s; on the test report's slow line WAV took 45-57 s, FLAC 38 s, MP3 12 s. When ffmpeg cannot make the
  FLAC the WAV goes as before; a run that replaced its work folder or left a link sends nothing. The 25 MB (about 13
  minutes) limit is still the WAV's. ffmpeg 8.1 does not replace an existing output without `-y` and still exits 0: the
  first build sent the first piece's MP3 again for the second; each piece's file now has its own name.
- **No tags.** ffmpeg copies a file's title and comment into the WAV's LIST chunk by default, and that WAV went to
  OpenRouter. The piece's WAV and voice input's WAV are made with `-map_metadata -1 -fflags +bitexact`.
- **Routing.** The request asks for `provider: {zdr: true, data_collection: deny, order: [deepinfra, groq], only:
  [deepinfra, groq], allow_fallbacks: true}` (`OPENROUTER_STT_PROVIDERS`, one constant): DeepInfra first, Groq when
  DeepInfra is down (the founder: a fallback, and the hosted key's guardrail allows these two), never a provider outside
  the list. It first asked for DeepInfra alone with fallbacks off, which would have left no fallback while DeepInfra is
  down once OpenRouter applies the field. OpenRouter's transcription endpoint ignores `only` today (a
  provider that does not exist was answered by DeepInfra; Groq still served 9 of the 87 requests of this test, 5 of
  the 41 the read path sent one at a time, and its retry of the QA meeting wrote invented Korean over two minutes of
  English),
  so a hosted key limits the providers with its own provider guardrail; the field takes effect the day OpenRouter applies it.
  The answer does not name the provider. The `media.transcribe` audit row now also holds `generations` (OpenRouter's
  generation id of each request, retries included) and `served` (requests by provider, `unknown` until known): the
  read looks each id up at OpenRouter (`GET /api/v1/generation`, the key in the header only, no sound or text, no
  redirects) about 8 s after the row is written, up to three tries, and fills `served` in that row (not when the chat
  was locked confidential during the read: nothing more goes to OpenRouter from it). No transcript words. Voice input
  has no audit row and none was added.

## Anthropic-compatible gateway (feat/anthropic-gateway, 2026-11-01)

A self-hosted team can run the real Claude Code engine on another company's models through an address that speaks
Anthropic's Messages API (OpenRouter; the Anthropic-compatible APIs of DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu): `engine.anthropicGateway`
in server.json (docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Anthropic-compatible gateway"). Before, a managed Linux install that pointed
`modelUpstreams.anthropic` at OpenRouter answered once two checks were relaxed (the key format and the Claude model
name; test of 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.305 on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, folder permissions held, eleven requests
upstream, no `claude-*` name among them). This makes it a supported setting instead of a test override.

- **server.json only, managed mode only.** `{ baseUrl, models: { default, opus?, sonnet?, haiku? }, label?, prices? }`;
  no admin screen. The server refuses to start with both `anthropicGateway` and `modelUpstreams.anthropic` /
  `modelUpstream` (two answers to where Claude requests go), outside managed mode (a local-login engine never uses the
  proxy), with a non-https address (http only to 127.0.0.1, like modelUpstreams: fake gateways in tests), with `/v1` at
  the end of the address (the proxy adds `/v1/messages`), or with a model id that is not argv-safe or is `claude-*`.
